item.title: How to use Base44 to build a working app for free
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On the Base44 home screen, say who the app is for, what it helps them do and why it is useful. Keep the first prompt to the core idea. Add details later. Pick Plan in the mode menu beside Build. Base44 asks about your users, the main flows and the design. Plan messages cost a fraction of a credit. The first build costs about 1. Sources: Base44 Docs: Quick start guide, Base44 Docs: Starting from your first prompt, Base44 Docs: Prompt guide, Base44 Docs: Billing and plans, Base44 Pricing, TechCrunch, Wix Press Room.

The Free plan gives 25 message credits a month, at most 5 a day, for up to 5 apps.","tags":["Base44","Wix","AI app builder","vibe coding","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Base44 is an AI app builder: you describe an app in plain language and it builds a working version, including the design, the database, user signups, permissions and hosting, with no code. If you want to know how to use Base44 to build an app for free, the short version is this: sign up, describe your idea, refine it in the AI chat, and click Publish.","sources":[{"name":"Base44 Docs: Quick start guide","url":"https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/Quick-start-guide"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Base44 was started by Israeli programmer Maor Shlomo and was about six months old, with roughly 250,000 users, when Wix agreed to buy it for about $80 million in cash on June 18, 2025, according to TechCrunch. Wix said the deal also includes earn out payments through 2029.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2025/06/18/6-month-old-solo-owned-vibe-coder-base44-sells-to-wix-for-80m-cash"},{"name":"Wix Press Room","url":"https://www.wix.com/press-room/home/post/wix-further-expands-into-vibe-coding-with-acquisition-of-base44-a-hyper-growth-startup-that-simplif"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Base44: your first build","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Sign up and write your first prompt","text":"After you sign up, the Base44 home screen shows one prompt box. Base44's prompt guide says a good first prompt covers three things: who the app is for, what it helps them do, and why that is useful. Keep it to the heart of the app. You can add every other feature later, and smaller requests also use fewer credits.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: A simple first build","text":"Build an expense tracker for freelancers who bill several clients. Users log an expense, tag it with a client and a category, and see monthly totals per client on a dashboard. Keep the design clean and calm, with one main page and a simple form.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"The AI may ask a few clarifying questions before it builds. You can skip them, or answer with a placeholder like [company name] and fill it in later. There is also speech to text if you would rather talk than type.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Use Plan mode when the idea is still fuzzy","text":"In the prompt box, open the Mode menu beside Build and choose Plan. Base44 then talks the idea through with you: what the app is for, who uses it and in which roles, the core flows, and the design. When the plan looks right, click Start Building. According to the docs, plan messages cost a fraction of a credit and the first build costs about 1 credit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Start from files, a website or a design if you have one","text":"The plus menu on the first prompt offers more ways in. Attach files from your computer or Google Drive: images and PDFs act as a visual reference, while spreadsheets and CSV files shape the data. Start from URL copies a site you own, as Content & Design or Design only. You can also import from Figma or pick connectors such as Google Workspace, Slack or GitHub.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start from URL does not copy private backend code, hidden data or third party integrations. Use it to rebuild the look and the public content, then add the logic with prompts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Refine the app without burning credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Learn the editor","text":"Once the first version is built, the editor shows the AI chat on the left and a live preview on the right. The top bar holds Edit mode, the Dashboard, version history and the publishing controls. Previewing the app is free; changes made through the chat cost credits based on the work and the model.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Ask for one change at a time","text":"Base44's own advice is to build in stages: get the core feature working, then add the next piece. Describe what the screen should show, say why, and ask for the fix rather than the flaw. Instead of saying the homepage looks cluttered, ask for fewer items per row and more space between sections.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Describe the screen you want","text":"Redesign the dashboard so it shows three cards at the top: total spent this month, number of expenses, and the client with the highest spend. Below them, add a bar chart of spending per month for the last 6 months. I want to see at a glance which client costs me the most.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Add logic, not just looks","text":"Only show the Delete button on an expense to the user who created it. When an expense is over [amount], mark it with a red label so it stands out in the list.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Use Select mode, Discuss mode and version history","text":"Select mode lets you click the exact element you want to change, and direct edits do not use credits. Discuss mode is for brainstorming: it talks through ideas without changing the app, and the docs say it uses fewer credits than building. Version history lets you restore an earlier version, so you can experiment without fear.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Plan a feature in Discuss mode first","text":"I want to add a booking flow where clients pick a time slot and get a confirmation email. Before you build anything, list the pages, the data you would store, and the steps a client goes through. Tell me what you would build first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Test and publish your Base44 app","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Test it like a real user","text":"Click through the preview the way a user would. Under More actions, Act as a user shows the app as a specific person or role. Base44 also suggests opening the app in a private browser window and on a phone. The device menu in the top bar switches the preview to mobile size.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Click Publish","text":"Click Publish in the top bar. The panel has Web and Mobile app tabs. From there you can edit the web address, share the app, set App visibility, check the Security status, and publish your latest changes. Get domain sets up a custom address. To take an app offline later, go to Dashboard, then Settings, then Danger Zone, then Unpublish App; your data and settings stay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If the chat shows Thinking for a long time, wait: the docs say detailed prompts can take 10 to 15 minutes. If it stalls, break the request into smaller prompts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the Base44 Free plan includes","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Free plan costs nothing and includes 25 message credits a month, with at most 5 a day, 100 integration credits a month, up to 5 apps, and core features such as authentication, a database and analytics. For apps created from October 18, 2026, each app's database is capped at 200 MB.","sources":[{"name":"Base44 Docs: Billing and plans","url":"https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Billing-and-plans"},{"name":"Base44 Pricing","url":"https://base44.com/pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Some things need a paid plan. Starter, listed at $16 a month billed annually, adds 100 message credits, unlimited apps, custom domains, private apps and the option to hide the Edit with Base44 badge on live apps. Builder, listed at $40 a month billed annually, adds code export to a ZIP file or GitHub, payments through providers like Stripe, and a choice of AI model.","sources":[{"name":"Base44 Docs: Quick start guide","url":"https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/Quick-start-guide"},{"name":"Base44 Docs: Starting from your first prompt","url":"https://docs.base44.com/Getting-Started/starting-from-your-first-prompt"},{"name":"Base44 Docs: Billing and plans","url":"https://docs.base44.com/Account-and-billing/Billing-and-plans"},{"name":"Base44 Pricing","url":"https://base44.com/pricing"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Five message credits a day go fast if you ask for one small tweak per message. On the Free plan, plan in Plan or Discuss mode, write clear requests that cover a whole screen, and use Select mode for small text and style edits. Base44 is a fast way to get a real, working prototype; just do not expect a free app with your own domain, private access or payments.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: ChatGPT agent mode is gone. Here is how to use what replaced it
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the new desktop app, pick Work in the menu, above Codex, Scheduled and Sites. Agent mode and /agent no longer exist. OpenAI's help page points here. Add Gmail, Drive, Slack or Outlook from the plugins directory. Type @ plus an app's name to pull it into the task. Describe the goal, your limits and the result you want. Sources: OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT agent, OpenAI: ChatGPT for your most ambitious work, OpenAI Help Center: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT, VentureBeat, OpenAI Community, OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT agent, The Next Web.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"ChatGPT agent mode is gone: how to use ChatGPT Work instead","dek":"Agent mode and the /agent command no longer exist. Here is what replaced them, how to start a task in ChatGPT Work and what it still cannot do.","summary":"OpenAI's help page for ChatGPT agent now says the feature is no longer available and points to ChatGPT Work. Work connects to your apps, builds slides, sheets and documents, and can run tasks on a schedule, but its cloud browser cannot sign in or pay.","seo_title":"ChatGPT agent mode is gone: how to use ChatGPT Work instead","seo_description":"ChatGPT agent mode no longer exists. How to use ChatGPT Work instead: open it, connect apps, run and schedule tasks, 4 prompts, and what it still cannot do.","answer_summary":"ChatGPT agent mode was retired in 2026 and OpenAI now points users to ChatGPT Work. Open Work from the menu in the ChatGPT desktop app (or on the web on eligible paid plans), connect your apps and describe the result you want.","tags":["ChatGPT","ChatGPT Work","OpenAI","AI agents","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"If you are looking for ChatGPT agent mode, you will not find it anymore. OpenAI's help page for ChatGPT agent now says the feature is no longer available, and it sends people to ChatGPT Work for long, multi-step tasks and finished files, and to the cloud browser inside Work for tasks on websites. This guide shows what replaced agent mode and how to use ChatGPT Work for the same jobs.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT agent","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Agent mode arrived in July 2025. You picked it from the tools menu or typed /agent in the message box, and ChatGPT worked on its own virtual computer with a visual browser, a text browser and a terminal. It could make editable slides and spreadsheets, asked before purchases and was trained to refuse high-risk tasks such as bank transfers. Plus and Business users got 40 agent messages a month and Pro users got 400, according to the old help article.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT agent","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent"},{"name":"OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT agent","url":"https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI never posted a single removal date. On August 8, 2026, a user on the OpenAI Community forum reported that agent mode was gone and that users were told to use Work instead, with no advance notice. An OpenAI support account replied on September 7 and apologized that the transition disrupted the user's workflow.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Community","url":"https://community.openai.com/t/agent-mode-was-removed-with-no-real-replacement/1389601"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What ChatGPT Work is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI launched ChatGPT Work on July 9, 2026. The company describes it as an agent that acts across your apps and files, works on a project for hours and turns a goal into finished work. It can create and edit slides, spreadsheets and documents, open Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 files, and run tasks on a schedule. On the desktop app it can also use a built-in browser and, with Computer Use, click, type and move files in the background.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: ChatGPT for your most ambitious work","url":"https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Work connects to other services through plugins, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars, CRMs and project trackers. VentureBeat reported that it runs on a persistent cloud virtual machine and can accept, decline or reschedule calendar events through those connections.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: ChatGPT for your most ambitious work","url":"https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/"},{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/openai-introduces-chatgpt-work-a-cloud-based-ai-agent-that-manages-tasks-across-email-slack-and-calendars"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Plans matter. OpenAI said Work reaches Pro, Enterprise and Edu first on the web and mobile, followed by Plus and Business. In the desktop app for Mac and Windows, Chat, Work and Codex are listed for every plan, including Free. The cloud browser is limited to paid plans other than Free and Go, in supported regions, and OpenAI says Work is still rolling out gradually to eligible accounts.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: ChatGPT for your most ambitious work","url":"https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/"},{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/20001280-using-cloud-browser-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use ChatGPT Work, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Open Work","text":"In the new ChatGPT desktop app, select Work in the app menu. It sits above Codex, Scheduled and Sites. On the web and in the mobile apps, Work appears for eligible paid plans. On mobile you can start a task, check progress and review drafts, then pick it up again on the web.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Connect the apps you need","text":"Open the plugins directory and add the services the task touches, such as Gmail, Google Drive, Outlook or Slack. ChatGPT may also suggest a plugin in the middle of a chat. To pull in context from a connected app, type @ followed by the app's name in your message.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Describe the outcome, not the clicks","text":"OpenAI's cloud browser guide asks for three things: the website, item or service; your constraints; and the result you want. A task like \"find a table for four near Union Square on Friday at 7 p.m. under $60 a person\" works better than \"search restaurants\".","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Answer its questions and approve big steps","text":"Work stops and asks before actions that are hard to undo or that create a financial, legal or account commitment. Before you confirm, check the site, the recipient or item, any price or account change and the exact action it proposes. You decide what it can reach and when it needs approval.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Review the result and where it came from","text":"When the task ends, read the output and the source pages before you rely on it. OpenAI notes that the last screenshot can sometimes come back blank even when the task finished.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Schedule it if it repeats","text":"Scheduled tasks can run once, on a schedule, or when something changes. Use them for things like a weekly summary of a shared folder or a daily check of a price or a status page.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts to copy","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Book-ready restaurant options","text":"Find three restaurants near [neighborhood] that have a table for [number] people on [day] at [time]. Keep it under [budget] per person and skip anything with fewer than 4 stars. Do not book anything. Give me the name, the open time slot and the link for each.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Track a package from your email","text":"Look in my connected email for the shipping confirmation from [store]. Open the carrier's public tracking page and tell me where the package is and when it should arrive. If tracking needs a sign-in, stop and tell me.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Turn files into a deck","text":"Use the files in @Google Drive folder [folder name] and the last two weeks of messages in @Slack channel [channel]. Make a 6-slide summary for [audience]: the goal, progress, numbers, risks and next steps. List the file each number came from.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A weekly check-in","text":"Every Monday at 8 a.m., check [page or folder] for changes since last week and send me a five-line summary. If nothing changed, say so in one line.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What it still cannot do","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The cloud browser cannot sign in to sites, take passwords, use autofill or password managers, or complete payments at launch, and a task that needs any of these stops. CAPTCHAs and sites that block automated access can also stop it, and some sites are blocked for safety or compliance reasons, so you may need to finish the last step yourself. On iPhone, a task can look stuck after you approve an action; reopening the conversation or continuing on the web fixes it.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/20001280-using-cloud-browser-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Usage follows the same model as Codex: there is no fixed message count, and complex tasks use more of your plan's allowance than simple ones. That is a change from agent mode's flat 40 or 400 messages a month.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI: ChatGPT for your most ambitious work","url":"https://openai.com/index/chatgpt-for-your-most-ambitious-work/"},{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT agent","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/11752874-chatgpt-agent"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Never paste passwords or card numbers into the chat. If a connected app can do the job directly, OpenAI recommends using the app instead of the browser, and it suggests stopping a task the moment it opens the wrong site.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Work also reads far more of your data than a normal chat does, which VentureBeat flagged as a privacy trade-off. You can remove saved browser data from the cloud browser in ChatGPT settings.","sources":[{"name":"VentureBeat","url":"https://venturebeat.com/technology/openai-introduces-chatgpt-work-a-cloud-based-ai-agent-that-manages-tasks-across-email-slack-and-calendars"},{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: Using cloud browser in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/20001280-using-cloud-browser-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Agent mode was a single tool you switched on for one task. Work is closer to a place you hand projects to: it keeps context across steps, connects to the apps you already use and can repeat a job on a schedule. The catch is that it still stops at sign-ins and payments, so the most useful tasks today are research, comparisons, drafts and files you review before anything goes out.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Google wants to make AI TV shows starring you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: A Google patent application describes "My Channel", a channel on your TV home screen full of AI-generated shows. You are the protagonist. The filing lists genres like a sci-fi adventure and a fun romantic comedy. A figure from Google's patent filing. The system could use photos or videos of you to make a digital likeness and a synthetic voice for your character. It would read your watch history and demographic data to pick the genre, themes and pacing. A screenshot from the patent filing. Sources: 404 Media, Gizmodo, Cointelegraph.

item.nf:article: {"headline":"Google patent filing describes AI-generated TV shows that star the viewer","dek":"The \"My Channel\" application would use watch history, photos and a synthetic voice to cast viewers in custom shows, with ads inserted.","summary":"A Google patent application published in November 2026 describes a TV channel of AI-generated shows in which the viewer is the protagonist, built from watch history and demographic data. A patent application filed in May 2025 describes the idea, and Gizmodo reported that the examiner rejected it, though Google can amend or appeal.","tags":["Google","AI video","Patents","Advertising"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"A Google patent application describes a system called \"My Channel\" that would fill a television channel with AI-generated shows built around a single viewer, who would appear as the main character, according to reports from 404 Media, Gizmodo and Cointelegraph published on November 23 and 24, 2026. The filing was first spotted by the patent tracking site Patentlyze, 404 Media reported.","sources":[{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"},{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/google-wants-to-make-ai-tv-shows-starring-you-2000844299"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Cointelegraph reported that Google submitted the application on May 13, 2025, and that the US Patent and Trademark Office published it in November 2026. The publication names two Google employees as inventors, Aravind Reddy Ayuluri and Prameela Kavya Thummuru, according to Cointelegraph. 404 Media gave the filing's title as \"creating a channel of video experiences tailored to a user.\"","sources":[{"name":"Cointelegraph","url":"https://cointelegraph.com/news/google-wants-make-you-star-your-own-ai-slop-movies"},{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How the channel would work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Gizmodo, the channel would sit on the TV home screen, and selecting it would bring up a set of show options personalized to the viewer's profile. The filing says shows could be created when a user asks for one or without a specific request, Gizmodo reported. The genres listed in the application include a sci-fi adventure, a romantic comedy, a crime and comedy caper and an action thriller, with a sample viewer named John cast as the protagonist, according to 404 Media.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/google-wants-to-make-ai-tv-shows-starring-you-2000844299"},{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"To personalize the content, the system would draw on the viewer's demographic data, video watch history and other information about the user, 404 Media reported. Gizmodo wrote that a language model would analyze the viewer's most watched videos and shows, and that the genre, themes, pacing, narrative structure and aspect ratio of each generated show would follow that viewing history.","sources":[{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"},{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/google-wants-to-make-ai-tv-shows-starring-you-2000844299"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Cointelegraph reported that the system could use photos or videos of the viewer to build a digital likeness and generate a synthetic voice for the character's dialogue. One example in the filing describes a viewer who watched highlights of a cricket player receiving a video that places the viewer at the Cricket World Cup, for instance cheering in the stands, according to 404 Media and Cointelegraph.","sources":[{"name":"Cointelegraph","url":"https://cointelegraph.com/news/google-wants-make-you-star-your-own-ai-slop-movies"},{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Advertising built in","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The application also covers advertising. According to Gizmodo and 404 Media, a finished show could be passed to an advertising stitcher that inserts at least one advertisement before the content reaches the viewer. Cointelegraph described the flow as an ad server retrieving the generated video, adding ads and streaming the result to the viewer's television.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/google-wants-to-make-ai-tv-shows-starring-you-2000844299"},{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"},{"name":"Cointelegraph","url":"https://cointelegraph.com/news/google-wants-make-you-star-your-own-ai-slop-movies"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The application has not been approved. Gizmodo, citing Patentlyze, reported that the patent examiner rejected it, though Google could still amend the application or appeal. None of the reports gave a date for the rejection. Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment from 404 Media or Gizmodo, and Cointelegraph said it had contacted the company.","sources":[{"name":"Gizmodo","url":"https://gizmodo.com/google-wants-to-make-ai-tv-shows-starring-you-2000844299"},{"name":"404 Media","url":"https://www.404media.co/google-wants-to-make-a-24-7-ai-tv-channel-youll-be-the-main-character/"},{"name":"Cointelegraph","url":"https://cointelegraph.com/news/google-wants-make-you-star-your-own-ai-slop-movies"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Patent filings often describe ideas that never become products, and nothing in the reports indicates that Google plans to launch a channel like this. item.title: How to use Freepik AI, now called Magnific, for images and video
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Open the Image Generator, write a prompt, choose a style, aspect ratio and model, or leave it on Auto. Then click Generate. item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Video in the Gemini app now needs a paid Google AI plan. Flow is free for adults in supported countries: open labs.google/fx/tools/flow in Chrome or Edge and sign in. item.title: Starting November 24, Wells Fargo says anything your AI agent does in your account is on you
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Wells Fargo's updated online banking terms take effect November 24. They say: "Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK." Whatever an agent does is treated as if you did it yourself, with no further checks. The terms say Wells Fargo does not monitor, screen or review what AI agents do in your account. Cut an agent off? Keep proof that you revoked its access, and hand it over if the bank asks. JPMorgan, Citi and Schwab block outside AI agents from logging in for customers. Sources: Wells Fargo, American Banker, AIM Media House, Hunton Andrews Kurth.

The help center gives a limit of 100 MB per file and up to 50 files in a session. Long context is Kimi's oldest strength: the first public version in 2023 already handled 128,000 tokens, and Kimi says K3 has a 1 million token context window.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Compare two long documents","text":"I uploaded two versions of the same contract. List every clause that changed between version 1 and version 2. For each change, quote the old and new wording and explain in one sentence what it means for [me / my company].","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Ask Kimi to quote the exact passage behind each answer when you work with a long file. It makes mistakes easy to spot, and you can jump straight to the page to check.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Save prompts you reuse","text":"Kimi lets you store prompts you use often. The help center calls them Presets on one page and Quick prompts on another. Save the ones you type every week, like a meeting summary format or a translation style.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Turn on Memory if you want Kimi to remember you","text":"With Memory switched on, Kimi can refer to its Memory Space and to your past chats when it answers. You manage what it keeps in the settings. Leave it off if you share the account or do not want past chats used.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Kimi Agent for bigger jobs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Kimi Agent is the part that does the work instead of chatting about it. Kimi says it plans a task, uses more than 20 built-in tools, including code, a terminal, a browser and image and audio generation, and hands back finished files. It grew out of OK Computer, the agent mode Kimi launched in September 2025.","sources":[{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Introducing Kimi Agent","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/agent/agent-overview"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Kimi (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_(chatbot)"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Open the agent and describe the task","text":"On the web, the agent lives at kimi.com/agent. In the app, Kimi's instructions are to pick K3 or K3 Swarm in the model switch above the chat box. Then describe the whole task in one message, including what you want delivered and in which format.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Watch the work, then download the result","text":"While the agent runs, you can follow its reasoning, the tools it calls, the websites it visits and the intermediate steps. When it finishes you get the deliverable: a code project, Word, PDF or Markdown documents, Excel or CSV sheets, slides, charts, or a deployed web page you can preview, download or share.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Turn a report into a slide deck","text":"Turn the PDF I uploaded into a 12 slide presentation for [audience]. One idea per slide, a short title, no more than 3 bullet points each, and a final slide with the 3 main takeaways. Deliver it as an editable PPT file.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Clean up a messy spreadsheet","text":"In the Excel file I uploaded, remove duplicate rows, fix the date column so every date uses the same format, and add a summary sheet with totals by [category] and a chart of the monthly trend. Return a new Excel file and tell me what you changed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"9. Use Deep Research for a long report","text":"Deep Research is one of the agent's modes. Kimi describes it as long-form research with complex search, multi-step reasoning and charts, and its help center has a prompt library sorted by use: industry research, competitor analysis, due diligence, legal research, academic work, policy and personal decisions.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Research before a big purchase","text":"Research [product category] for someone who [your situation]. Compare the 5 best options on price, reliability, and what owners complain about most. End with a clear recommendation and the 3 sources you trusted most.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For heavier jobs, Kimi also lists Agent Swarm, which it says can coordinate up to 300 sub-agents and more than 4,000 tool calls, Kimi Code, a command line tool and VS Code extension for programmers, Kimi Claw, a cloud agent it says starts in under 30 seconds, and Kimi Work, a desktop agent for Mac and Windows.","sources":[{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Kimi overview","url":"https://www.kimi.ai/help/getting-started/overview"},{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Kimi overview (kimi.com)","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/new-user-guide/overview"},{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Introducing Kimi Agent","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/agent/agent-overview"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Kimi costs and where it falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Wikipedia, the Kimi apps are free with general rate limits, and paid plans named Moderato, Allegro, Allegretto and Vivace raise those limits and speed up agent tasks. The help pages used for this guide do not list prices, so check the membership page inside Kimi before you pay. Deep Research tasks use credits, according to Kimi's own FAQ list.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: Kimi (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_(chatbot)"},{"name":"Kimi Help Center: Deep Research","url":"https://www.kimi.com/en/help/deep-research"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Two things to know before you trust it with work data. Moonshot AI is based in Beijing, so read the privacy terms with that in mind. And Kimi K3 has faced accusations, including from the director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, that it was built by distilling Anthropic's Claude, according to Wikipedia.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: Kimi (chatbot)","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kimi_(chatbot)"},{"name":"Wikipedia: Moonshot AI","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moonshot_AI"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Kimi is a strong pick for long documents, slides and spreadsheet work, and its agent is generous for a free app. Like every chatbot, it can be confidently wrong, so check numbers and quotes against the source before you send anything Kimi made.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Best Lovable prompts to build an app faster (8 to copy)","dek":"Eight copy and paste prompts built on Lovable's own docs, for planning, design, login, scoped changes and bug fixes that do not waste credits.","summary":"Eight Lovable prompts based on Lovable's prompting best practices, prompt library and debugging guide. Each one asks for one change, names where it goes and says what must stay the same.","seo_title":"Best Lovable prompts: 8 to copy for building apps faster","seo_description":"8 Lovable prompts to copy: make it ask questions first, pick a design, add login, lock what must not change, report bugs and turn fixes into project rules.","answer_summary":"Good Lovable prompts ask for one change at a time, name the page or component, describe the result you want and say what must not change. For big changes, use Plan mode or ask Lovable to ask you questions before it builds.","tags":["Lovable","Prompts","Vibe coding","AI app builder","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"The best Lovable prompts are short, scoped and specific. They say what to build, where it goes and what must stay the same. This guide collects eight prompts built on Lovable's own documentation: its prompting best practices, its prompt library and its debugging guide. Fill in the [brackets], send one prompt at a time and check the result before the next one.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Why this matters: every build costs credits, and Lovable fills any gap in your prompt with its own guesses. LowCode Agency founder Jesus Vargas, in a prompting guide updated on October 16, 2026, says those guesses are often wrong. His fix is four parts in every prompt: the current state of the project, the exact page or component, the result the user should see, and what must not change.","sources":[{"name":"LowCode Agency: Lovable prompting guide","url":"https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/lovable-prompting-guide"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you are new to Lovable, start with our guide on how to use Lovable to build an app without coding. This one assumes you already have a project open.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Best Lovable prompts for planning","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Make Lovable ask you questions first","text":"I want to add [feature] to my app. Before you build anything, ask me any questions you need to fully understand what I want from this feature.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting best practices recommend closing a prompt with a request for clarifying questions, and say this works especially well in Plan mode. The prompt library gives the same advice for large prompts: ask Lovable to check its questions first, or use Plan mode to agree on the approach before it builds.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Have Lovable rewrite your prompt","text":"Here is a prompt I plan to send you: [paste your prompt]. Rewrite it to be clearer and more specific: name the pages, the components and what must not change. Do not build anything yet.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompting handbook calls this meta prompting: you ask the AI to refine your prompt before you use it. The same handbook recommends scoped edits, where you tell the AI to change only certain files or sections and leave other pages alone.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Blog: The Lovable prompting handbook","url":"https://lovable.dev/blog/2025-01-16-lovable-prompting-handbook"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"A rewrite costs one message and often saves several. A vague prompt like \"make the dashboard better\" can turn into a long chain of fixes, while a rewritten version names the cards, the chart and the table you actually want.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Three design directions before building","text":"Describe three different design directions for the hero section of [your app] before you build anything. For each one, give the style, the colors and the fonts.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompt library includes a prompt that asks for three directions for the hero section before anything is built, plus ready-made style prompts for minimal, glassmorphic, bold, playful, calm and editorial looks. Its best practices page suggests picking the style early and saving your chosen keywords in the project's instructions so every later prompt uses them.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for building features","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Add login the right way","text":"Add sign up, log in and forgot password pages that match the app's current style. Require login before the dashboard. Add a Sign in with Google button next to email and password. Show clear error and success states on every form.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"This is based on the sign up and login prompt in Lovable's prompt library, which runs on Lovable's built-in backend. The library says each of its prompts is meant to work as a single Build mode message, and that some features need a paid plan: payments need Pro or higher, and email alerts need a paid plan.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use real words, not placeholder text. Lovable's best practices say real headlines and button labels show layout problems early, and that you should plan for logged-in and logged-out states and for empty, loading and error states.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Lock what must not change","text":"Only change the [page or component]. [The change you want]. Do not touch the login flow, the payment code or any other page. When you are done, tell me which files you changed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's best practices tell you to set boundaries: what to build, where it goes and what must stay unchanged, with \"only change the orders page\" as an example. Its debugging guide adds that guardrails for fragile areas such as authentication or payments belong in the same prompt as the task.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompting best practices","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-one"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for fixing bugs","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Report a bug Lovable can fix","text":"On the [page name] page, [what is broken]. I expected [what should happen], but instead [what happens]. Here is the exact error: [paste error]. This worked before [your last change]. What is the root cause? Explain it in simple terms before you change any code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's debugging guide describes a bug in four parts: what is broken, where it happens, what you expected and what happened instead. Add a screenshot for layout problems and the exact error text. Lovable reads console logs from the preview on its own, but errors on the published site have to be pasted in.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The guide says to use the Try to fix button once or twice when an error appears. Accounts get 10 free fixes, and each one comes back 24 hours after it is used. If the same error keeps returning, switch to Plan mode and find the root cause first, because repeated blind fixes tend to hide the real problem.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Test the whole flow in the browser","text":"Use browser testing to check that [the flow, for example sign up to checkout] works from start to finish. If something fails, reproduce it, fix it and test it again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's prompt library has prompts that ask it to use browser testing to check a flow such as checkout, and to reproduce a bug in the browser, fix it and then confirm the fix. It also includes a security review prompt that checks the login flow and whether API routes are secure.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Docs: Prompt library","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-library"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 8: Turn the fix into a project rule","text":"We just fixed [the bug]. Summarize what went wrong, what we tried and the fix that worked, as a short rule I can add to the project instructions so this does not happen again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Lovable's handbook calls this reverse meta prompting, and its debugging guide gives the same advice: after a hard bug, ask Lovable to summarize the problem and the fix so it can go into project instructions. Instructions, previously called Knowledge, are read with every message. You set them in Project settings, then Instructions, with a limit of 10,000 characters.","sources":[{"name":"Lovable Blog: The Lovable prompting handbook","url":"https://lovable.dev/blog/2025-01-16-lovable-prompting-handbook"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Instructions (Knowledge)","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/features/knowledge"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What these prompts cannot fix","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Good prompts do not remove every limit. Vargas writes that if three targeted corrections fail on the same issue, the cause may be a limit of the platform rather than the prompt. Lovable's own debugging guide suggests restoring a working state from version history, or editing an earlier message and choosing Revert and resend, then telling Lovable what you did.","sources":[{"name":"LowCode Agency: Lovable prompting guide","url":"https://www.lowcode.agency/blog/lovable-prompting-guide"},{"name":"Lovable Docs: Debugging prompts","url":"https://docs.lovable.dev/prompting/prompting-debugging"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The pattern behind all eight prompts is the same: one change per message, a clear place, a clear result and a clear limit. Plan first when the change is big, and write down what worked so the next prompt starts from it. That is slower for the first ten minutes and faster for the rest of the project.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use GPTZero (and how accurate AI detectors are)","dek":"How to run a GPTZero scan, read the AI probability and confidence score, check a Google Doc's writing history, and what independent tests say about accuracy.","summary":"GPTZero scans pasted text or uploaded files and says whether it looks AI written, human written or mixed, with a probability and a confidence level. The free plan covers 10,000 words a month, and GPTZero itself says a result should not be the only proof of AI use.","seo_title":"How to use GPTZero and read its AI detection score","seo_description":"How to use GPTZero: paste or upload text, press Scan, read the AI probability and confidence level, check sentence highlights and know its accuracy limits.","answer_summary":"Go to gptzero.me, paste your text or upload a file and press Scan. Read the result as a probability that the whole text is AI, human or mixed, check the confidence level, and treat it as a starting point, not proof.","tags":["GPTZero","AI detector","AI writing","Education","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero is an AI detector: you give it text, and it tells you whether the text looks written by AI, by a human, or by both. If you want to know how to use GPTZero, the short version is: paste the text on gptzero.me, press Scan, then read both the percentage and the confidence line. The tool was built by Edward Tian, then a Princeton undergraduate, and launched in January 2023.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero","url":"https://gptzero.me/"},{"name":"Wikipedia: GPTZero","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPTZero"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The scan takes seconds. Reading the result correctly is the hard part, and it matters most when the result is about someone else's work. This guide covers both, plus what independent testers found about accuracy.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use GPTZero, step by step","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Paste your text or upload a file","text":"Open gptzero.me. The homepage has a text box with a limit of 10,000 characters; for longer scans, GPTZero says to create a free account first. Besides pasted text, GPTZero says it accepts DOCX, PDF and image files. The free plan allows up to 3 files in a batch upload.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Press Scan","text":"GPTZero's own instructions are short: paste raw text or upload your file and press Scan. The Basic AI Scan on the free plan returns an overall AI detection score for the document.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Read the label and the percentage","text":"Each result sorts the text into AI, human or mixed, and shows an AI probability. That percentage is not the share of the text that is AI. It is the model's probability for the whole document. GPTZero's example: a 4% AI result means that out of 100 similar cases, about 4 would be fully AI written, about 57 mixed and about 39 fully human.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check the confidence level","text":"Under the score, GPTZero says how sure it is. Highly confident means an error rate under 2%, moderately confident means around 10%, and low confidence means 14% or higher. GPTZero says that when the model is unsure, it leans toward human with a low confidence score.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Look at the sentence highlights","text":"Advanced Scan shows which sentences and phrases affect the score most, ranked as high, medium or low impact. Sentences that are not highlighted can still affect the result, because the detector reads the text as a whole. The free plan includes one Advanced Scan to try it; the full feature is part of the Premium plan.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Scan longer passages when you can. GPTZero says its model performs best on longer texts and English prose, so a single paragraph gives a weaker signal than a full essay.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Scan Google Docs with the browser extension","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero's browser extension works in Chrome, Edge and Firefox. GPTZero's Chrome page says it is free to install with a GPTZero account and comes with a monthly allowance of scans, highlighting sessions and chat messages, which paid plans raise. It can scan webpages when you ask it to, and in Google Docs it can scan automatically, color sentences by AI confidence and replay how the document was written.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero Support: Google Docs writing report","url":"https://support.gptzero.me/articles/7001890416-what-is-the-google-docs-writing-report-for-origin"},{"name":"GPTZero: Chrome extension","url":"https://gptzero.me/chrome"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Watch a writing report","text":"Install the extension and log in. Open a Google Doc you can edit, then click Watch Writing Report in the GPTZero menu. The report replays the writing process and evaluates whether the typing pattern looks human. If you only have view access, the menu asks you to request edit access. The free plan has a usage limit on writing reports.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you write your own work in Google Docs, the writing report is your best defense against a false flag: it shows the document being typed, edited and pasted over time, which a single score cannot.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the free and paid plans include","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to GPTZero's support center, the free plan includes 10,000 words a month, up to 10,000 characters per scan, the Basic AI Scan and one Advanced Scan. Essential adds Grammar Check, AI Vocabulary Check and scans up to 50,000 characters. Premium adds the full Advanced Scan, Writing Feedback, Plagiarism Check and batches of up to 50 files. Professional adds LMS integration, scans up to 150,000 characters and batches of up to 250 files.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero Support: Free and paid plans","url":"https://support.gptzero.me/articles/1272562776-what-is-the-difference-between-the-free-and-paid-for-plans"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero's support article does not list prices. PCWorld's review, published November 16, 2026, listed Premium at $23.99 a month, or $12.99 a month billed annually, with 300,000 words a month, and Professional at $45.99 a month, or $24.99 a month billed annually, with 500,000 words a month. PCWorld also noted that the free version may use your text for training.","sources":[{"name":"PCWorld: GPTZero review","url":"https://www.pcworld.com/article/3278225/gptzero-review.html"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How accurate GPTZero really is","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"GPTZero says it keeps its false positive rate, human text wrongly flagged as AI, at no more than 1%, and reports 96.5% accuracy on documents that mix human and AI writing. It says its false positive rate on essays by non-native English speakers from the TOEFL exam is 1.1%. These are the company's own benchmarks. GPTZero also states that no AI detector is 100% accurate and that a result should be a conversation starter, not the final verdict.","sources":[{"name":"GPTZero: AI detection technology","url":"https://gptzero.me/technology"},{"name":"GPTZero: AI accuracy benchmarking","url":"https://gptzero.me/news/ai-accuracy-benchmarking"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"PCWorld ran 50 samples in five groups. GPTZero scored all 10 pure AI samples, from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, as 100% AI, and all 10 human samples as 0% AI. The weak spot was AI text edited by a person: one such sample scored 96% human and another 98% human. Results on human text lightly edited with AI were inconsistent.","sources":[{"name":"PCWorld: GPTZero review","url":"https://www.pcworld.com/article/3278225/gptzero-review.html"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Older research is less kind to detectors in general. A Stanford study led by James Zou tested seven detectors, GPTZero among them, on 91 TOEFL essays and found that on average they classified 61.22% as AI generated, while they were near perfect on essays by U.S. eighth graders. The researchers also showed that asking a chatbot to rewrite text in more literary language helped it evade detection. GPTZero says it has since trained on more ESL writing.","sources":[{"name":"Stanford HAI: AI detectors biased against non-native English writers","url":"https://hai.stanford.edu/news/ai-detectors-biased-against-non-native-english-writers"},{"name":"Liang et al.: GPT detectors are biased against non-native English writers","url":"https://arxiv.org/html/2304.02819v3"},{"name":"GPTZero: AI accuracy benchmarking","url":"https://gptzero.me/news/ai-accuracy-benchmarking"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Early reporting raised the same worry. According to Wikipedia's summary, Futurism wrote in January 2023 that, based on the error rate it saw, teachers relying on the tool could falsely accuse nearly 20 percent of innocent students, and The Washington Post noted in August 2023 that even a small false positive rate could lead to wrongful accusations.","sources":[{"name":"Wikipedia: GPTZero","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GPTZero"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"GPTZero is good at the easy cases: raw chatbot output and plainly human writing. It is weaker when a person has reworked AI text, and every detector's error rate becomes a real person once you scan a whole class. Use it as a screening tool, read the confidence line, scan full documents, and back any concern with a writing report or a conversation before you decide anything.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: OpenAI's chief scientist wants every AI lab to agree on a shared speed limit for smarter models
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Jakub Pachocki argues most benchmarks are outdated, but perplexity, a score for how well a model predicts the next token, still tracks progress. Lower means better predictions. GPT-4 scored about 0.91 on OpenAI's measure. Below 0.8, the post says, models showed transformative skills in cybersecurity and math. Labs would agree not to cross a shared limit until monitoring catches up. Sam Altman called the post the most important thing OpenAI has published in a while. Sources: TechCrunch, Datastudios.

TechCrunch reported on the post that afternoon, and Datastudios published a detailed summary of its figures.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"},{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman praised the post on X, describing it as the most important thing the company had published in a while, according to TechCrunch.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Why perplexity","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pachocki argues that benchmarks built around specific downstream tasks have gone out of date as models improved, while perplexity has stayed informative. Perplexity measures how well a model predicts the next token on average, and a lower score means better predictions. TechCrunch reported that the post includes a chart showing how the perplexity of OpenAI's models has fallen since GPT-3.5.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"According to Datastudios, the figures are log-perplexity scores measured on a held-out dataset drawn from OpenAI's internal codebase. GPT-3.5 sat at roughly 0.99 and GPT-4 at roughly 0.91. Pachocki wrote that GPT-4 was able to use chain-of-thought reasoning productively at that level, and that once OpenAI's models reached losses below 0.8, the company saw transformative capabilities emerge in fields such as cybersecurity and mathematics.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"},{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Datastudios reported that the post also cites an unnamed OpenAI model at about 0.76, linked to strong results on open math problems, and expects further capability jumps somewhere around 0.68 to 0.7. The post does not say which model reached 0.76 or whether the lower range would serve as a limit.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What the proposal asks of AI labs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pachocki suggests that perplexity could act as a shared benchmark for general intelligence, which companies could use to set common limits. Under the idea, developers would commit not to go past an agreed threshold until their ability to understand and monitor AI behavior reaches a concrete milestone, TechCrunch reported.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Datastudios described the plan in three layers: shared norms for evaluating and red-teaming frontier models before first use, along with transparency standards; commitments not to cross common limits defined by perplexity and other measures until a monitoring milestone is met, with a successor to chain-of-thought monitors given as an example; and a framework for setting later limits. The post names no partner companies and no date for a first limit, and it announces no change to ChatGPT, Codex or the API, according to Datastudios.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The post also lists open problems, Datastudios reported. Labs train on different datasets, perplexity does not map directly onto real tasks, gains from chain-of-thought reasoning do not lower perplexity, and nobody knows where the loss floor lies. OpenAI said it is publishing its own numbers as a first step, while acknowledging that this gives competitors a clearer view of its progress.","sources":[{"name":"Datastudios","url":"https://www.datastudios.org/post/openai-proposes-perplexity-limits-frontier-ai-development"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The wider push for limits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The proposal arrives as calls for restraint grow inside the industry. TechCrunch noted that Anthropic's IPO filing warned the technology could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society, and that Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei has published a plan to pace the frontier, calling for common safety standards and limits on the rate of unchecked AI progress. Altman and Elon Musk reportedly endorsed that plan.","sources":[{"name":"TechCrunch","url":"https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/22/openais-chief-scientist-has-thoughts-on-how-to-limit-ai-development/"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The notable part is less the idea of limits than the choice of a single number to define them. A shared metric would let rival labs check one another, but only if they agree on the dataset it is measured on, a problem the post itself raises. By publishing its own scores first, OpenAI is betting that openness will pull competitors into the same frame.","sources":[]},{"kind":"why_it_matters","text":"The test is whether Anthropic, Google DeepMind, xAI or Meta publish comparable perplexity figures or sign on to a common threshold. Without that, the proposal remains one company's yardstick.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to delete your Meta AI chats for good
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the Meta AI app, tap Menu at the top left, then Settings at the bottom left. Under App settings, tap Data & privacy, then Manage your information. Confirm with Delete all. Your chats, prompts and media leave the History and Media sections. On meta.ai, click your profile picture, then Settings and the same path. Sources: Meta Help Center: Remove posts, chats and media from Meta AI and Vibes, Meta Help Center: Manage your information on Meta AI and Vibes, The Washington Post (via The Nightly): Your AI chatbot keeps a file on you, Meta Help Center: Meta AI and Vibes.

item.title: AI godfather Yann LeCun says Anthropic's Dario Amodei hypes AI dangers so he can stay in control
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On November 22, LeCun answered an X post about Amodei's remarks to a US congressional hearing. He wrote that Amodei has hyped the dangers since GPT-2 so that open models would be made illegal and he would stay in control. Yann LeCun, founder of AMI Labs. LeCun compared it to the Ottoman Empire banning the printing press for Arabic to keep control of the dogma. He called it "a new form of medieval obscurantism" and said Amodei left OpenAI because he "wasn't going to have control." Sources: OfficeChai, The Open Press, NewsBytes.

item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Kling 4.0 makes clips of 3 to 30 seconds in one pass, with up to 10 keyframes. Its Omni Reference takes up to 15 assets: images, videos, subjects and voices. item.title: How to use Grok Imagine for AI images and video
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Go to grok.com/imagine or open the Grok app on iPhone or Android. For pictures, pick Quality Mode. That is where the new Image 2.0 model runs. item.title: Players caught AI-made music hidden in The Binding of Isaac's new update
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: The November 19 update added a GTA-themed daily run called Crime Mode. A Reddit user checked its music files and found Suno metadata in them. The Steam page had no AI disclosure. None of the reports identified who made or added the tracks, and GamesRadar+ said there was no word yet on how they got into the game.","sources":[{"name":"ShiftDelete.Net","url":"https://shiftdelete.net/en/binding-of-isaac-ai-music-removed"},{"name":"Power Up Gaming","url":"https://powerupgaming.co.uk/2026/11/21/binding-of-isaacs-gta-6-ai-music/"},{"name":"Steam","url":"https://store.steampowered.com/app/3353470"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"The response from McMillen and Nicalis","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Edmund McMillen, the game's original creator and lead designer, wrote on X that he had no idea the daily run featured generated music and that he was looking into how it happened and getting it removed. PC Gamer noted that Nicalis licenses the game from its creator and that many players blamed the publisher.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/roguelike/the-binding-of-isaac-removes-ai-generated-music-from-new-update-and-designer-edmund-mcmillen-is-looking-into-how-that-happened/"},{"name":"PC Gamer","url":"https://www.pcgamer.com/games/roguelike/binding-of-isaac-dlc-adds-ai-music-in-gta-6-parodying-update-despite-not-having-an-ai-disclosure-steam-reviews-drop-to-overwhelmingly-negative-music-gets-pulled/"},{"name":"Power Up Gaming","url":"https://powerupgaming.co.uk/2026/11/21/binding-of-isaacs-gta-6-ai-music/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Nicalis released a patch on PC that removed the generated music files and also fixed bugs, improved netcode and restored compatibility for mods. The patch was submitted to Microsoft, Nintendo and Sony, with no console release date given, according to GamesRadar+ and ShiftDelete.Net.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/roguelike/the-binding-of-isaac-removes-ai-generated-music-from-new-update-and-designer-edmund-mcmillen-is-looking-into-how-that-happened/"},{"name":"ShiftDelete.Net","url":"https://shiftdelete.net/en/binding-of-isaac-ai-music-removed"},{"name":"Power Up Gaming","url":"https://powerupgaming.co.uk/2026/11/21/binding-of-isaacs-gta-6-ai-music/"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Steam showed recent reviews for Repentance+ as Overwhelmingly Negative on November 23, with 8% of 1,205 reviews from the previous 30 days positive. Overall reviews stood at Mixed, at 50% positive. Reviews quoted by the outlets also complained about new bugs in the update.","sources":[{"name":"GamesRadar+","url":"https://www.gamesradar.com/games/roguelike/the-binding-of-isaac-removes-ai-generated-music-from-new-update-and-designer-edmund-mcmillen-is-looking-into-how-that-happened/"},{"name":"Steam","url":"https://store.steampowered.com/app/3353470"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The episode shows how quickly players now check for generated assets, and how little it takes to find them when tool metadata is left in the files. You can use one of its stock avatars, animate a photo, or build a digital twin from a short video of yourself. Write the script, scene by scene","text":"A scene is a block of script plus the avatar and anything else on screen. Type your script in the text field. Record your training footage","text":"Go to Avatar, then Avatars, click New Avatar and choose Clone a real person. Record the consent video","text":"HeyGen will not let you make videos with a twin until it verifies consent. An optional Custom Motion prompt describes gestures.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Custom Motion prompt to try","text":"Speaks calmly to the camera, nods once at the start, and uses small open hand gestures at chest height. Keeps both hands below the chin.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What HeyGen costs in practice","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Paid plans run on credits. Business is $149 a month for the first seat. Unused credits on monthly plans carry over for one more billing cycle, and they are lost if you cancel down to Free.","sources":[{"name":"HeyGen Help: Credit based pricing plans explained","url":"https://help.heygen.com/en/articles/15125761-heygen-credit-based-pricing-plans-explained"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The model you pick changes the bill. It is weaker the moment you need hands, movement or long scenes. Start on the free plan with a stock avatar, test a 30 second script on the model you plan to use, and only pay once you know how many minutes a month you really make.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use Descript: edit your video by deleting words from the transcript
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Descript transcribes your file and links the text to the media. Select words and press Delete to cut them from both. Changed your mind? Right click the edit and choose Restore removed media. In the AI Tools panel, choose Remove filler words to find every um and uh in the script. item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use Descript to edit video by editing text","dek":"Descript turns your recording into a transcript that stays linked to the video, so cutting words cuts the footage. Filler word removal sits in the AI Tools panel, and the free plan covers 60 media minutes a month.","tags":["Descript","AI video editing","Underlord","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Descript is a video and audio editor that transcribes your recording and keeps the transcript linked to the media, according to its help center. Create a new project","text":"From your drive, click New project in the top right corner and choose the type of project. New projects save to your personal private workspace unless you are on an Enterprise plan and choose a different one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add your media","text":"Upload a video, audio or image file from your computer, or bring files in from another project, your drive's Media Library, Zoom cloud recordings or, in Descript for Web only, Google Drive. The Activity panel shows upload progress, and canceled uploads are not charged media minutes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Put the file in the script","text":"Uploaded files appear under Files in the Project panel on the right. When you add a file to the script, Descript transcribes the speech so you can edit by text. You can also use files as timeline layers for B-roll, visuals or background music.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to edit video by editing the transcript","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Delete words to cut the video","text":"Select text in the script and press Delete or Backspace. The words disappear from the transcript and the matching audio and video disappear with them. Editing is non-destructive: to bring something back, right click the edit boundary and choose Restore removed media.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Move sections with cut and paste","text":"Cut a passage with Command X on a Mac or Ctrl X on Windows, click where it should go and paste with Command V or Ctrl V. The media moves with the text. Copy instead of cut if you want to duplicate a section.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Fix the transcript","text":"Use Correct your transcript to fix typos, wrong words and speaker labels. If you need precise timing, for captions or sync fixes, the wordbar lets you adjust where each word starts and ends. Ignore strikes through text but keeps it visible in the script, and Remove from transcript hides text from the script, captions and exported transcripts while leaving the media in place.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To mark a laugh, a cough or another sound that is not speech, type an opening parenthesis, the note and a closing parenthesis. Inline notes show up in exported transcripts. For feedback to a teammate, use comments instead.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to remove filler words in Descript","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Run Remove filler words","text":"Open the AI Tools panel in the right sidebar and choose Remove filler words. A sidebar lists each detected filler word with a timestamp, and the words are underlined in light blue in the script. Preview them, then choose Delete, Delete and replace with gap to keep the timing, Ignore, or Remove from transcript.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Turn on Avoid harsh cuts before you apply the removal. Descript then skips filler words it cannot remove without clipping the words around them. Filler word detection works only on English transcripts and uses AI credits on current plans. To clean only part of a video, duplicate that section to a new composition, run the tool there and paste the result back.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Underlord, the AI co-editor","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Underlord is Descript's AI co-editor, still labeled beta. You open it from its icon in the right sidebar of any project and type requests, such as adding captions, cutting clips, translating, adding zooms and fades or applying Studio Sound at a set intensity. The model selector near the bottom of the chat lets you pick a model, and premium models need a paid plan.","sources":[{"name":"Descript Help: Underlord","url":"https://help.descript.com/getting-started/underlord-beta-your-ai-co-editor-in-descript.md"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Find short clips for social","text":"Find the best 60 to 90 second moments in this video and turn each one into a vertical clip for social media.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Add styled captions","text":"Add social style captions to this video in [your brand color], with a bold font and a dark background behind the text.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Clean up the audio","text":"Apply Studio Sound at [intensity] to the speaker track and lower the other audio so the speech stands out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Each Underlord prompt uses AI credits, and when it runs a tool you pay for both the reasoning and the tool, with costs that vary between runs of the same prompt, according to the help center. Descript also says plainly that Underlord can overpromise, make wrong assumptions or try workflows it cannot finish, and that it works best when you check its output as you go.","sources":[{"name":"Descript Help: Underlord","url":"https://help.descript.com/getting-started/underlord-beta-your-ai-co-editor-in-descript.md"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Descript plans and limits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The Free plan costs nothing and includes 60 media minutes a month, 100 one time AI credits and 720p exports with a watermark, according to the pricing page. Hobbyist is $16 per person a month billed annually or $24 monthly, with 10 media hours, 400 AI credits a month and 1080p export. Creator is $24 billed annually or $35 monthly, with 30 media hours, 800 credits and 4K export. Business is $50 billed annually or $65 monthly, with 40 media hours and 1,500 credits. Sonix lists the same prices and allowances in its review.","sources":[{"name":"Descript: Pricing","url":"https://descript.com/pricing"},{"name":"Sonix: Descript Review 2026","url":"https://sonix.ai/resources/?p=3512"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Studio Sound, Remove Filler Words and Underlord are limited on the Free plan and included on the paid ones. Transcription covers 25 languages on every plan. Cloud storage runs from 5GB on Free to 2TB on Business.","sources":[{"name":"Descript: Pricing","url":"https://descript.com/pricing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Descript is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Transcripts are not perfect. Zapier's tutorial says the transcript is fairly accurate but sometimes gets things wrong. Sonix, a competing transcription company, estimates accuracy at about 92 to 95 percent for clean single speaker English, lower with heavy accents or three or more speakers, and says Descript is designed for recordings under 60 minutes. Sonix also says AI credits do not roll over, and that heavy use of Studio Sound and Underlord can use up the Creator plan's 800 credits.","sources":[{"name":"Zapier: How to use Descript","url":"https://zapier.com/blog/descript-review"},{"name":"Sonix: Descript Review 2026","url":"https://sonix.ai/resources/?p=3512"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Descript is at its best on spoken content: podcasts, interviews, tutorials and talking head videos. The text editing alone saves real time, and it works on the free plan. The weak spots are the meters. Media minutes and AI credits both run out, Underlord can burn credits on retries, and filler word removal is English only. Read the transcript before you cut, do simple trims by hand, and save the AI tools for jobs that would take you longer.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: Cursor limits explained: what every plan really gets
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk

item.title: Amazon is close to a $7.5 billion AI deal
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Amazon is in advanced talks to buy San Francisco startup Decart at a valuation of about $7.5 billion, the Financial Times reported on November 21. A deal could come within days, though talks could still collapse. Amazon declined to comment. Decart, founded in 2023, makes software that helps AI models run more efficiently and frees up chip capacity. It was an early user of Amazon's Trainium chips, which Amazon built to compete with Nvidia's GPUs. Sources: PYMNTS, Seeking Alpha, GeekWire, The Seattle Times via The Spokesman-Review.

Captions and basic edits work on the free plan, but AI features such as AI Edit, eye contact and caption styles need a paid plan to export.","tags":["Captions","Captions AI","AI video editing","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Captions is an AI video editor built by Mirage, a New York AI research company, and it runs on iPhone, Android and the web at captions.ai, according to its help center. Its own docs recommend a single speaker, say captions work best on clips of 60 to 90 seconds, and suggest keeping imported footage under three minutes for AI Edit.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: AI Edit","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/project/ai-edit"},{"name":"Captions Help: Add captions","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/captions/add-captions"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use Captions AI Edit on your phone","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Update the app","text":"AI Edit is rolling out on iOS, according to the help center. If you do not see it, update the app first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Start an Edit project","text":"On the Home screen, keep Edit selected and add your media. Choose the options","text":"Pick a model, then review Inputs and options: the aspect ratio, a Voiceover only toggle, and the output shape, Portrait 9:16 or Landscape 16:9. Check the credit estimate and create","text":"Before you start, Captions shows an estimated range of credits. Fix things by hand when you can","text":"Manual edits on the timeline use no credits.
