Captions says you can start dubbing for free, while Lipdub is a premium feature.","sources":[{"name":"Captions: AI Dubbing","url":"https://captions.ai/features/ai-dubbing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Eye Contact is a tool in the app's editing panel that corrects your gaze after recording, for talking head footage. AI Twin creates an avatar of you from a short recording where you read a script; Captions lists it as a Max plan feature and recommends recording in a quiet room.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: Export","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/settings/export.md"},{"name":"Captions: AI Twin","url":"https://captions.ai/features/create-ai-twin"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Captions AI plans and credits","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free plan includes basic tools such as trim, transitions, zoom and sound effects, one caption template and no AI credits, according to the pricing page. Max costs $24.99 a month with 500 credits. Frontier costs $69.99 a month with 1,400 credits, and Frontier 2x and 4x cost $139.99 and $279.99 for 2,800 and 5,600 credits. Captions says these prices reflect its iOS plans. An independent review by eesel AI lists the same prices and credit amounts.","sources":[{"name":"Captions: Pricing","url":"https://captions.ai/pricing"},{"name":"eesel AI: Captions AI features, pricing and limitations","url":"https://www.eesel.ai/blog/captions-ai"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Unused credits roll over to the next month, up to three times your monthly allowance, according to the credits page. Individual top ups are not available on standard plans, and canceling forfeits the remaining credits at the end of the period.","sources":[{"name":"Captions Help: Credits","url":"https://captions.ai/help/docs/troubleshooting/credits.md"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Export","text":"Tap Export, choose your settings and tap Export again. Advanced options include resolution, frame rate, bitrate and a separate SRT caption file. Basic manual edits export free, but the help center says AI features such as AI Edit, caption styles, eye contact correction and background music need a paid subscription, and the app asks for one when you export.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Captions is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Try your edit on the free plan before you pay. You only find out at export that a feature you used needs a subscription, so it is worth knowing which tools are AI features first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Captions is built for short videos of one person talking. The help center itself steers you toward clips of a minute or two, and the five minute caps on translation and dubbing rule it out for long interviews. The eesel AI review also points to a learning curve and to app store complaints about lag, captions going out of sync after edits and crashes at export. Credits make the monthly cost hard to predict if you lean on chat edits and high effort levels, so start with Quick and do small fixes by hand.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Perplexity prompts: 7 to copy for faster research","dek":"Seven copy and paste prompts built on Perplexity's own help center tips, for quick answers, comparisons, Deep Research reports and files.","summary":"Seven Perplexity prompts based on the tips in Perplexity's help center. Each one adds context, asks for one thing and names the format, and three of them use Deep Research or file creation, which depend on your plan.","seo_title":"Perplexity prompts: 7 to copy and paste for faster research","seo_description":"7 Perplexity prompts to copy: ask with context, compare options, run Deep Research, analyze your own file and turn the results into a spreadsheet or deck.","answer_summary":"Good Perplexity prompts state one clear goal, add a line of context, use the keywords that matter and name the format (a table, bullet points or steps). For long reports, use Deep Research from the plus (+) menu, which Perplexity includes on Pro, Max and Enterprise plans.","tags":["Perplexity","Prompts","AI search","Deep Research","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"These Perplexity prompts come from Perplexity's own help center, which lists the habits that get better answers: say what you want, give context, ask for one thing at a time and name the format. Below are seven prompts built on those tips, with [brackets] where your details go. Paste one in, fill the brackets, and you get a cited answer instead of a pile of links.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"},{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Practical tips for using Perplexity","url":"https://intercom.help/perplexity-ai/en/articles/10352971-how-can-i-use-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity's help center describes a good prompt as five parts: an instruction, context, the input, keywords that matter, and the output format you want. You do not need all five every time, but most weak answers miss at least two of them. The help center gives \"Cars.\" as an example of a search that is too vague to be useful.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Practical tips for using Perplexity","url":"https://intercom.help/perplexity-ai/en/articles/10352971-how-can-i-use-perplexity"},{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts for everyday research","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: The question with context","text":"I'm a [who you are] in [where you live]. [Your question, as one clear sentence]. Give me the answer as [a table / bullet points / a step by step guide].","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"This is the base pattern, and every other prompt here is a version of it. Perplexity's own example is a first-time homebuyer in the US asking which federal programs can help. The context line changes the sources it picks, and the format line saves you from reformatting the answer yourself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Compare two options","text":"Compare the pros and cons of [option A] vs. [option B] for [your situation]. Put the result in a table with one row per point, and note which sources disagree.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Add the keywords that actually decide the answer. The help center's example is \"best noise-canceling headphones under $200 for commuting\": the price and the use case do more work than the word headphones.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Arguments for and against","text":"Summarize the main arguments for and against [idea or decision], with supporting data. Keep each side to five points and link the source for every number.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity's help center uses a four-day work week as its example for this one. It works for anything people argue about: a policy, a purchase, a career move. Asking for a fixed number of points per side keeps the answer balanced and short enough to read.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts for Deep Research","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Deep Research reads many sources and writes a detailed report. According to Perplexity's help center, it is included on Perplexity Pro, Perplexity Max, Enterprise Pro and Enterprise Max. To start it, open the plus (+) menu in the search bar and pick Deep Research; on the web you can also type / in the search bar. Perplexity notes the menu can look different depending on the platform.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: A full report on one question","text":"Research [topic] and [what you want it to suggest or explain], including [the detail you care about most, for example cost comparisons].","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Be clear about what you want to learn before you hit enter. Perplexity's sample is \"the environmental impact of fast fashion and sustainable alternatives, including cost comparisons\". The help center contrasts it with \"Tell me about fashion\", which gives Deep Research nothing to aim at.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Narrow it down","text":"Now focus on [one part of the report]. What does the evidence say, and where is it weak?","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Start broad, then narrow with follow-ups in the same thread, as the help center recommends. Its example is a report on remote work trends in the United States since 2020, followed by \"Now focus on the impact on employee productivity.\" One big question and two short follow-ups usually beat one giant prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Your file plus the web","text":"Based on the attached [report, contract or spreadsheet] and the latest [market data or news], what's the outlook for [company, product or plan]? Separate what comes from my file and what comes from the web.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Perplexity's help center says you can upload your own files and ask Deep Research to analyze them next to web sources, using an attached financial report as its example. The last sentence of the prompt above is our addition: it makes it easier to see which claims came from your document.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Perplexity prompts that make a file","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Turn research into a document, deck or sheet","text":"Build a spreadsheet comparing the top [5] [tools or products] by [price], [features] and [user ratings].","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Depending on your plan, Perplexity can create documents, slide decks and spreadsheets, and the help center says documents include citations. Say the file type plainly, for example \"Create a Word document\", \"Build a slide deck\" or \"Make a spreadsheet\", and describe the structure, such as a 10-slide presentation with sections on budget, channels and key metrics. Documents export as .pdf or .docx, presentations as .pptx and spreadsheets as .xlsx.","sources":[{"name":"Perplexity Help Center: Tips for getting better answers","url":"https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13645819-tips-for-getting-better-answers-from-perplexity"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Fix the file with short follow-ups instead of rewriting the prompt. The help center's examples are \"Add a conclusion slide\" and \"Make the executive summary shorter.\" You can also run a search first and then ask Perplexity to turn the results into a document or deck in the same session, if your plan includes file creation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to write your own Perplexity prompts","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Start with one clear goal","text":"Write the question you would ask an expert, not a search keyword. Asking for the current inflation rate in the US works; \"inflation\" makes Perplexity guess.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Add who you are and why you ask","text":"One sentence of background is enough. Perplexity's tips and the University of Florida Business Library's guide both point out that context and follow-up questions are what turn a generic answer into a useful one.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Ask for one thing and name the format","text":"A table, bullet points or a step by step guide. If you need three things, ask three times in the same thread.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Test and tweak","text":"Perplexity's help center tells users to test prompts and adjust them. If the answer misses, change one part of the prompt (the context, the keywords or the format), not all of it at once.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Perplexity falls short","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Perplexity is only as good as the question. Vague prompts get vague answers, and the help center says so with examples like \"Cars.\" and \"Write something for me.\" Usage limits depend on your plan, the help center lists Deep Research only for Pro, Max and Enterprise plans, file creation also depends on the plan, and every regenerated or edited image counts as a new generation toward your image limit. The citations make it easy to check an answer, so open at least one source for any number you plan to reuse.","sources":[]}]}

Here is how to start, how keyframes and Draft mode save credits, and what each plan includes.","summary":"Luma AI's Dream Machine makes short videos from text or images with its Ray3 family of video models. Draft mode gives fast, cheaper previews, and paid plans start at $30 a month for 10,000 credits on Luma's current price list.","seo_title":"How to use Luma AI Dream Machine: Ray3, credits and plans","seo_description":"How to use Luma AI Dream Machine: make a video from a photo with keyframes, test in Draft mode, write Ray3 prompts, and see what credits and each plan cost.","answer_summary":"Sign in to Dream Machine, upload a photo as the start frame (or type a prompt), turn on Draft mode to get quick previews, then upgrade the clip you like to full quality. Luma's price list charges Ray3.14 clips by length and resolution, for example 100 credits for 5 seconds at 720p.","tags":["Luma AI","Dream Machine","Ray3","AI video","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"Dream Machine is Luma AI's app for making videos and images with AI. Pick text or a photo","text":"You can start from a text prompt (text to video) or from an image (image to video). Luma's Ray3 FAQ says the model does best with image to video, so if you have a good photo, start there. You get more control over how the first frame looks, and fewer wasted tries.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Set keyframes","text":"In the Keyframes tab you can set a start frame, an end frame or both, and Dream Machine fills in the motion between them. Each frame can be uploaded or made in Dream Machine first. Turn on Draft mode","text":"Switch on the Draft toggle in the composer window. Luma's Ray3 guide says drafts come back up to 5x faster, and its price list charges much less for draft generations. Use drafts to try different prompts and camera moves.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Upgrade the one you like","text":"When a draft looks right, upgrade it to the full quality version, which Luma calls Hi-Fi. According to Luma's prompting guide, the same prompt style works in both, so you do not need to rewrite anything.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Choose HDR only if you need it","text":"HDR is not switched on by default: you select it in the Dynamic Range dropdown in the settings panel. Luma's Ray3 FAQ says HDR and EXR downloads are limited to 540p and 720p and cost more credits, so leave it off unless you are grading the footage in a video editor.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Luma's FAQ suggests generating at 720p and upscaling afterward if you need a bigger file, instead of paying for a higher resolution on every try.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to write a Ray3 prompt","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Luma's help center recommends writing prompts like stage directions for a film, in a set order: the camera and its movement, the subject and the action, the setting, how materials and physics behave, the lighting and mood, and finally the style. The Ray3 FAQ adds that clear prompts of two to four sentences work best.","sources":[{"name":"Luma AI Help: How do I use Ray3 prompting effectively?","url":"https://lumaai-help.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/151000223059-how-do-i-use-ray3-prompting-effectively-"},{"name":"Luma AI: Ray3 FAQ","url":"https://lumalabs.ai/learning-hub/ray3-faqs"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt: A clip from a product photo","text":"Slow push-in movement toward the [product] on a wooden table. Calm, realistic commercial style.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt: A locked camera scene","text":"Fixed viewpoint with no camera movement. A [person or animal] walks slowly across a [place] from left to right. Wind moves the grass and their clothes. Golden hour light, natural colors.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Credits and plans","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Everything in Dream Machine costs credits. On Luma's current price list, a Ray3.14 text or image to video clip costs 20 credits for 5 seconds at 360p, 100 credits at 720p and 400 credits at 1080p; a 10 second clip at 720p costs 300 credits. Plus costs $30 a month, or $25 a month billed yearly, with 10,000 credits and commercial use. Pro costs $90 a month with 40,000 credits, and Ultra costs $300 a month with 150,000 credits. Monthly credits do not roll over. On a paid plan you can buy top up credits, starting at $4 for 1,200 credits, which last 12 months.","sources":[{"name":"Luma AI: Plans and Pricing","url":"https://lumalabs.ai/learning-hub/dream-machine-support-pricing-information"},{"name":"Luma AI: Dream Machine credit system","url":"https://lumalabs.ai/learning-hub/dream-machine-credit-system"},{"name":"eesel AI: Luma AI pricing (2026)","url":"https://eesel.ai/blog/luma-ai-pricing"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Luma's subscription page describes a free tier limited to Photon images and draft resolution Ray3.14 video, with watermarks and for personal projects only. Luma's help center says videos made on the Free and Lite tiers carry a watermark, and that a clip made before upgrading stays watermarked; you have to generate it again to get a clean copy. Dream Machine credits and Luma's developer API are billed separately.","sources":[{"name":"Luma AI: Payments and subscriptions","url":"https://lumalabs.ai/learning-hub/payments-subscriptions"},{"name":"Luma AI Help: How do I use Ray3 prompting effectively?","url":"https://lumaai-help.freshdesk.com/support/solutions/articles/151000223059-how-do-i-use-ray3-prompting-effectively-"},{"name":"Luma AI: Plans and Pricing","url":"https://lumalabs.ai/learning-hub/dream-machine-support-pricing-information"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"To cancel, open your profile panel and choose Manage Subscription. Luma says you keep access until the end of the billing period, and that refund requests within 30 days go to its support email.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"What it is bad at: Luma's own Ray3 FAQ says character consistency can vary, including shifts in a person's apparent age or gender between shots, and that extended, looped or keyframed clips sometimes have abrupt transitions. The same FAQ says Ray3 does not make sound, so plan to add audio in an editor. Clips are short, five to ten seconds per generation in that FAQ, so longer videos mean extending or stitching several shots. Check the credit cost on screen before every Hi-Fi generation, because prices differ a lot by model and resolution.","sources":[]}]}

You can type @ to pick a saved skill, ask for a file as the result, or attach files with Upload and tools: upload a file, add one from Drive, or add a notebook. Then click Submit.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Steer it while it works","text":"Type more instructions at any time. Google says Gemini updates its work without losing progress. A progress chip at the top of the thread opens a panel with completed, current and planned steps, plus any files it made.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you are not sure how to phrase a task, type set up, get started or interview me, and Gemini will ask you questions to build it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Clean up your inbox","text":"Go through my Gmail from the last 30 days. Summarize the newsletters I never open, archive them, and list which ones I should unsubscribe from. Ask me before you unsubscribe from anything.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Watch a price","text":"Track hotel prices in [city] for [dates]. Alert me if a room under [budget] per night appears.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to schedule a Gemini task","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A task can have a schedule: tell Gemini when to run it, in the same text box. Google's own example is a daily 8 AM update on AI news; another is a Monday Brief at 9:00 AM that recaps your email and adds a to-do list. You can have up to 15 tasks running at the same time, and a scheduled task will not start if 15 are already running.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Manage your tasks and workflows","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/17094507?hl=en"},{"name":"Google: Tasks in Gemini","url":"https://gemini.google/overview/agent/"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: A weekly brief","text":"Every Monday at 9:00 AM, recap my email from the past week, list anything I still need to answer, and make a to-do list for the week.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Pause or resume a schedule","text":"Open the task thread, click the scheduled task chip, then More options, and choose Pause or Resume. The Scheduled page on the web lists them too.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Gemini asks before it acts","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Google says Gemini is designed to ask for your review before sending messages, deleting your data, sharing sensitive information, making purchases, completing financial transactions, or filling out and submitting web forms. Very sensitive actions need your permission every time, even if you change your preferences. The first time a task browses the web, Chrome asks to connect its auto browse feature to Gemini.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Manage your tasks and workflows","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/17094507?hl=en"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"With your permission it can use Gmail, Calendar, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Keep, Google Tasks, Maps, Flights, Hotels and YouTube, plus more than 50 third party apps such as OpenTable and Instacart. Those app connections are off by default. Android Central reports that calling local businesses for you is rolling out in the US first.","sources":[{"name":"Gemini Apps Help: Manage your tasks and workflows","url":"https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/17094507?hl=en"},{"name":"Google: Tasks in Gemini","url":"https://gemini.google/overview/agent/"},{"name":"Android Central","url":"https://www.androidcentral.com/apps-software/ai/google-just-made-its-best-gemini-agent-free-heres-where-you-can-get-it"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Never type a password or card number into the task thread. When a site needs them, Gemini asks you to take control of the browser so you can type them on the site yourself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to stop a task or turn Tasks off","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Stop one task","text":"Click Stop in the Gemini text box. If Gemini is browsing in Chrome, you can also click Stop in the Gemini side panel, or click View live and then Take over task to finish it yourself.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"Turn task mode off","text":"On the web, open Settings, then Task settings, and turn off Use task mode to hand off work. On a Mac, it is under Gemini, Settings, Tasks. Your schedules pause and your tasks and files are kept, so you can switch it back on later.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"What it is bad at: it can make mistakes and do unexpected things, in Google's own words, and some websites block it and hand the last step back to you. Hidden instructions in a web page or email could also try to steer it, which Google warns about. Start with low stakes jobs like inbox cleanup and price alerts before you trust it with anything that spends money or sends mail in your name.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use OpenClaw: your own AI assistant in Telegram and WhatsApp
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: On Mac or Linux the docs give a one line install script. It installs Node if needed and starts setup. Pick Quick start: it reuses a Claude Code or Codex login or an API key you already have. Make a bot with @BotFather, then add its token with one OpenClaw command. Strangers get a pairing code. Nothing runs until you approve them. Sources: OpenClaw Docs: Getting started, OpenClaw Docs: Install, OpenClaw Docs: Telegram setup, OpenClaw Docs: Pairing, OpenClaw Docs: Security, OpenClaw Docs: Why OpenClaw, Malwarebytes: OpenClaw, what is it and can you use it safely?.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to use OpenClaw: install it, connect Telegram and keep it safe","dek":"OpenClaw is a free, open source AI assistant that runs on your own machine and talks to you in your chat apps. Here is the setup, step by step, and the safety settings that matter.","summary":"OpenClaw is an open source AI assistant that runs on your own hardware and connects to chat apps like Telegram, WhatsApp and Discord. Setup takes one install command, but because it can run commands and read files, it needs careful limits.","seo_title":"How to use OpenClaw: install, Telegram setup and safety","seo_description":"How to use OpenClaw: install it with one command, finish onboarding, open the dashboard, connect a Telegram bot and lock down who can message your agent.","answer_summary":"Install OpenClaw with its one line installer, choose Quick start to reuse an existing Claude Code, Codex or API key login, then run openclaw dashboard to chat. To use it from your phone, create a Telegram bot with @BotFather and add the token with openclaw channels add.","tags":["OpenClaw","AI agents","Telegram","Open source AI","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenClaw is an open source AI assistant that runs on your own hardware and answers you in the chat apps you already use, according to its documentation. It runs a Gateway on your machine, works with many AI models, and has no paid tier. If you want to know how to use OpenClaw, the short version is: install it with one command, reuse an AI login you already have, then connect a chat app like Telegram.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Why OpenClaw","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/why-openclaw"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"It is not a toy. Malwarebytes describes OpenClaw as an agent that can browse the web, run shell commands, read and write files and chain skills together without a human checking each step. That is why it is useful, and why the safety section of this guide matters more than the install. The project was earlier known as ClawdBot and then Moltbot, Malwarebytes reported.","sources":[{"name":"Malwarebytes: OpenClaw, what is it and can you use it safely?","url":"https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/openclaw-what-is-it-and-can-you-use-it-safely"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What you need before you start","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs list two requirements. You need Node.js 24.16.0 or newer on the 24 line, or 26.1.0 or newer, and Node 26 is the recommended version. You also need some way to reach an AI model: an existing Claude Code or Codex CLI login, or an API key from a model provider. OpenClaw itself is free; the AI model you connect is what you may pay for.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Install","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/install"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Check your Node version first with node --version. If Node is missing, the installer script can set it up for you on macOS and Linux.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to use OpenClaw: install and first chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Run the installer","text":"On macOS, Linux or WSL2, the docs give this command: curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash. On Windows PowerShell it is iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex. The script detects your system, installs Node if needed, installs OpenClaw and starts onboarding. If you would rather just try it first, npx openclaw@latest runs it without the installer.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Choose Quick start","text":"Onboarding offers Quick start and Custom setup. Quick start looks for a Claude Code or Codex login or an API key you already have, checks that it works with a real request, saves the config and opens the web dashboard. If nothing it finds works, it switches to manual provider setup. You can change settings later with openclaw configure.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Keep it running in the background","text":"In Quick start the Gateway runs in your terminal until you press Ctrl+C. To keep it running, stop it and run openclaw gateway install. That installs a background service: a LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user unit on Linux and WSL2, or a Scheduled Task on Windows. Your config is kept.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Check it and open the dashboard","text":"Run openclaw gateway status and you should see the Gateway listening on port 18789. Then run openclaw dashboard. It opens the Control UI in your browser, where you can type a message and get a reply from your assistant.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"On Windows, the docs recommend the native Windows Hub companion app as the easiest path. There is also a macOS menu bar app if you prefer a normal app download over the terminal.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Connect OpenClaw to Telegram","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The docs call Telegram the fastest channel to set up, because it only needs a bot token. Other channels include Discord, iMessage, Microsoft Teams, Signal, Slack and WhatsApp.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Telegram setup","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/telegram/setup"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Create a bot with BotFather","text":"Open Telegram and start a chat with @BotFather. Check that the handle is exactly @BotFather. Send /newbot, follow the prompts and save the token it gives you.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Give OpenClaw the token","text":"Run openclaw channels add --channel telegram --token followed by your bot token. Then run openclaw channels status --probe to confirm Telegram is ready. Telegram does not use a login command; the token is all it needs.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Approve your first message","text":"Send any message to your bot. With the default pairing policy, that message is not processed. Instead it creates a pairing request. Run openclaw pairing list telegram, then openclaw pairing approve telegram with the code shown. Codes expire after one hour.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Pairing is OpenClaw's approval step for who may talk to your agent. Unknown senders get a short code and their message is ignored until you approve it. You can also approve requests in the Control UI under Settings, Channels, DM access requests. Approving a direct message does not give that person access in groups.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Pairing","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/channels/pairing"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to keep OpenClaw safe","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The OpenClaw docs say the defaults are conservative: on a normal install the Gateway only listens on your own machine, most chat channels answer unknown senders with a pairing code, and group access is allowlisted. The same docs are clear that sandboxing is off by default. They offer one command to check your setup: openclaw security audit.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Security","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/gateway/security"},{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Why OpenClaw","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/why-openclaw"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outside researchers are more cautious. Malwarebytes reported problems including prompt injection, exposed instances and a growing ecosystem of dubious third party plugins, and noted that the Dutch data protection authority warned organizations not to run experimental agents like OpenClaw on systems with sensitive data. Its advice, based on Microsoft's recommendations, is to run such agents in a sandboxed virtual machine or container, give them their own limited accounts, and treat every new skill as new code.","sources":[{"name":"Malwarebytes: OpenClaw, what is it and can you use it safely?","url":"https://www.malwarebytes.com/blog/news/2026/02/openclaw-what-is-it-and-can-you-use-it-safely"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Do not install OpenClaw on the laptop that holds your bank, work and password manager logins. Use a spare machine, a virtual machine or a container, connect only the accounts it needs, and install skills only from sources you trust.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"If OpenClaw does not work","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Run openclaw triage. The docs say it runs read only health checks and writes a cleaned up description of the problem, then offers to hand it to a coding agent such as Claude Code or Codex. Secrets, tokens and raw logs are left out. To read the findings yourself, run openclaw doctor instead.","sources":[{"name":"OpenClaw Docs: Getting started","url":"https://docs.openclaw.ai/start/getting-started"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"OpenClaw is a good fit if you are comfortable in a terminal and want an assistant you control, on your own hardware, reachable from your phone. It is a poor fit if you want something that is safe with no thought: an agent that can run commands needs the same care as any program you give admin rights. Start small, with one channel, one model and no sensitive accounts, and widen access only when you trust what it does.","sources":[]}]}

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"Claude Code prompts: 8 to copy and paste for real projects","dek":"Eight prompts built on Anthropic's own Claude Code advice, for understanding a codebase, fixing bugs, building features and reviewing changes.","summary":"Eight copy and paste Claude Code prompts based on the patterns in Anthropic's documentation. Most of them give Claude a way to verify its work, such as a failing test or a build that has to pass.","seo_title":"Claude Code prompts: 8 to copy and paste for real projects","seo_description":"8 Claude Code prompts to copy and paste: explore a codebase, plan in plan mode, fix bugs with a failing test, write tests and review changes with a subagent.","answer_summary":"The best Claude Code prompts are specific and include a way to check the result: name the files, describe the symptom, and ask for a failing test or a passing build. Plan larger changes in plan mode (Shift+Tab) first, and use /clear between tasks.","tags":["Claude Code","Claude","Prompts","AI coding","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"These Claude Code prompts come from the patterns Anthropic recommends in its own Claude Code documentation, rewritten with [brackets] so you can paste them into your own project. The short version: give Claude a way to check its work, plan before it codes, and be specific about files and the result you want. Vague prompts get vague code.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"},{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Common workflows","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Anthropic's best practices page makes one point above the rest: Claude does better when it can verify its own work, with a test to run, a build that has to pass, or a screenshot to compare against. Most prompts below build that check into the request.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Claude Code prompts for understanding a codebase","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Get the lay of the land","text":"Give me an overview of this codebase. Explain the main architecture patterns and the key data models, then tell me which files handle [feature].","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"You can point at files directly with @, for example @src/utils/auth.js. Typing @ opens a menu of paths, and Anthropic's docs note it also loads the CLAUDE.md files from that folder and its parents.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Plan before code","text":"I want to add [feature]. Read [folder] first. What files need to change? Create a plan before writing any code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"How to turn on plan mode","text":"Press Shift+Tab until the status bar shows that plan mode is on, or start a session with claude --permission-mode plan. In plan mode Claude reads and proposes but does not edit. Press Ctrl+G to edit the plan in your own editor, then approve it or press Shift+Tab to leave. Anthropic says to skip planning for changes you could describe in one sentence, because it adds overhead.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for fixing bugs","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Fix a bug the right way","text":"Users report that [what goes wrong]. Check [folder]. Write a failing test that reproduces the issue, then fix it and run the tests again.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The failing test is the important part. It proves the bug exists, and when it passes you know the fix did something. Without it you are trusting Claude's word.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 4: Fix the build, not the symptom","text":"The build fails with this error: [paste error]. Fix it and confirm the build passes. Fix the root cause, do not suppress the error.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for building features","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 5: Copy your own patterns","text":"Look at how [existing component] is built to understand our patterns. Follow the same pattern to build [new component]. Use only libraries already in this codebase.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 6: Let it interview you","text":"I want to build [short description]. Interview me in detail about the implementation, UI, edge cases and tradeoffs. Skip obvious questions. When we are done, write a full spec to SPEC.md.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Anthropic suggests building from the finished spec in a fresh session, so the long interview does not fill the context Claude needs for the code.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Prompts for tests and review","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 7: Fill the test gaps","text":"Find the functions in [file] that are not covered by tests. Add tests for them, including edge cases, then run the new tests and fix any failures.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 8: Get a second opinion","text":"Use a subagent to review the changes against [PLAN.md]. Check that every requirement is implemented and the edge cases have tests. Report gaps, not style preferences.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"A subagent works in its own context, so the review is not shaped by the session that wrote the code. Anthropic's docs warn that reviewers tend to over-report, which is why the prompt asks for gaps and not style. When you are happy, a plain request to commit with a descriptive message and open a pull request finishes the job.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"},{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Common workflows","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/common-workflows"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Setup that makes every prompt work better","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Run /init","text":"The /init command writes a starter CLAUDE.md, a file Claude reads at the start of every session. Keep it short: the test commands, the stack, and rules Claude keeps getting wrong. Anthropic's test for each line is whether removing it would cause mistakes.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Use /clear between tasks","text":"Performance drops as the context window fills, and Claude can start forgetting earlier instructions. Clear the session when you switch tasks, and if you have corrected Claude twice on the same thing, Anthropic suggests clearing and starting over with a better prompt.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Name your stack","text":"SitePoint's guide to Claude Code workflows recommends writing the exact versions of your frameworks into CLAUDE.md, because without them Claude may invent imports or use the wrong version of an API. It also warns against putting secrets in CLAUDE.md, since the file is usually committed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Where Claude Code still struggles","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Long sessions are the weak spot. Anthropic's docs say a single debugging session can use tens of thousands of tokens, a bloated CLAUDE.md makes Claude ignore instructions, and checkpoints only track edits made through Claude's file tools, so they are no substitute for git. SitePoint suggests starting a new session after three or four chained steps.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Code Docs: Best practices","url":"https://code.claude.com/docs/en/best-practices"},{"name":"Anthropic Engineering: Claude Code best practices","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/claude-code-best-practices"},{"name":"SitePoint: Claude Code workflows","url":"https://www.sitepoint.com/claude-code-workflows-a-practical-pattern-guide/"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Small, specific tasks with a clear check at the end beat one giant prompt. If a prompt has no way for Claude to prove it worked, add one.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to use OpenRouter: one API key for hundreds of AI models
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: Sign in, open Keys and click New Key. You can name it, set a credit limit and an expiry date. Copy the key right away and keep it in a password manager. In the chat playground, add the Free Models Router. It picks a free model at random for each request. 50 free requests a day, 1,000 once you have bought 10 credits. Here is how to get a key, try the free models, connect your code and avoid the surprises.","summary":"OpenRouter is a single API for hundreds of AI models that works with the OpenAI SDK. For free use, pick a model ending in :free or the openrouter/free router, which allows 50 requests a day, or 1,000 after you have bought 10 credits.","tags":["OpenRouter","AI API","Free AI models","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenRouter gives you access to hundreds of AI models through one API endpoint, one account and one credit balance, according to its documentation. Create an account","text":"Go to openrouter.ai and choose Get API Key, then sign in or create an account. A third party walkthrough by Merge notes you can log in with OAuth, email and password, or a passkey. Making an account and a key is free; you only pay when you use paid models.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Make a key","text":"Click New Key. A pop up lets you name the key, set an optional credit limit, choose whether that limit resets on a schedule such as weekly or monthly, and set an expiry date. A limit is worth setting on any key you put into a script or share with a tool.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Copy and store it","text":"Copy the key and keep it in a password manager. Your code sends it as a Bearer token in the Authorization header. You can check a key's remaining credit and limits with a GET request to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/key.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Use one key per app or tool, each with its own credit limit. If a key leaks, you lose that limit, not your whole balance.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Try OpenRouter free models first","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Many models have a free variant, marked with :free at the end of the model ID, with its own rate limits. There is also a Free Models Router, with the model ID openrouter/free, which picks a free model at random for each request and filters for features your request needs, such as reading images or calling tools.","sources":[{"name":"OpenRouter Docs: FAQ","url":"https://openrouter.ai/docs/faq"},{"name":"OpenRouter Docs: Free Models Router in the playground","url":"https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/get-started/free-models-router-playground.md"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Test it in the playground","text":"Open the chat playground at openrouter.ai/chat, click Add Model, type free and select Free Models Router. Send a message, and the reply shows which model answered. Chat room conversations are stored on your device and do not sync across devices.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The free limits: 20 requests a minute and 50 requests a day if you have bought less than 10 credits in total, and 20 a minute and 1,000 a day once you have bought at least 10. The higher tier counts what you have ever bought, not your current balance, so it stays even after you spend the credits. Failed attempts count toward the daily quota, and making extra accounts or keys does not raise the limits. Free models can also be throttled by their providers at busy times.","sources":[{"name":"OpenRouter Docs: FAQ","url":"https://openrouter.ai/docs/faq"},{"name":"OpenRouter Docs: Limits","url":"https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/reference/limits.md"},{"name":"OpenRouter Help Center: Rate limits","url":"https://openrouter.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/39501163636379"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you list paid models as fallbacks next to openrouter/free, those paid models are billed at their normal price. Point the OpenAI SDK at OpenRouter","text":"OpenRouter follows the OpenAI API format, including the chat completions and responses endpoints. In the OpenAI SDK, set the base URL to https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 and use your OpenRouter key as the API key. Then pass any model ID from openrouter.ai/models. Two optional headers, HTTP-Referer and X-OpenRouter-Title, put your app on OpenRouter's public rankings.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Example: a first request with curl","text":"curl https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses \\\n -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\\n -H \"Authorization: Bearer $OPENROUTER_API_KEY\" \\\n -d '{ \"model\": \"openrouter/free\", \"input\": \"Hello!\" }'","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Set stream to true to get the answer as it is written. Paid models have no request cap from OpenRouter itself, though the providers behind them can still throttle. If you hit a free limit, you get a 429 error; honor the Retry-After header when it is there.","sources":[{"name":"OpenRouter Docs: FAQ","url":"https://openrouter.ai/docs/faq"},{"name":"OpenRouter Docs: Limits","url":"https://openrouter.ai/docs/api/reference/limits.md"},{"name":"OpenRouter Help Center: Rate limits","url":"https://openrouter.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/39501163636379"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"OpenRouter fees, credits and privacy","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"OpenRouter charges a 5.5% fee, with a $0.80 minimum, when you buy credits, and 5% when you pay in crypto. Consensus combines keyword and semantic search over titles and abstracts, then re-ranks the top 1,500 papers using recency, citation count and journal reputation, then re-ranks the top 20 with a larger model. Ask a real research question","text":"Consensus works best with questions that academic papers actually study. Keywords work, and so do simple questions, such as whether statins are effective in elderly populations. It is not built for general knowledge questions. Consensus's own example of what not to ask is the capital of Germany.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Use a yes or no question to get the Consensus Meter","text":"Yes or no questions turn on the Consensus Meter, which shows how the papers lean. Oregon State's library guide says the meter appears when at least 5 papers directly answer your question.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: a question that triggers the Consensus Meter","text":"Does [treatment or habit] improve [outcome] in [group of people]?","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Pick a search mode","text":"Consensus has three modes. Quick analyzes 10 papers and gives a short summary, good for a fact check. Pro analyzes 20 papers and gives a detailed summary with custom formats, good for coursework and literature reviews. Deep analyzes 50 papers and writes a full report with diagrams and tables, meant for thesis work.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: a comparison table in Pro mode","text":"Create a table comparing the effectiveness of [approach A], [approach B] and [approach C] for [problem], with the study type and sample size for each finding.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to narrow and check the results","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Add filters","text":"Open the filter button next to Export. The filters in Consensus's guide are Journal Rank, Countries, Publish Year, Methodology, Sample Size, Study Durations, Fields of Study and Citations. You can set them before or after a search. SMU's library found that filtering for a discipline works well, while asking for a discipline in the question does not.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Use Boolean search for precise results","text":"Consensus supports AND, OR and NOT in capital letters, quotes for exact phrases and parentheses for grouping. Consensus's guide says a checkmark means the full text was analyzed. No checkmark means the summary came from the abstract only.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Consensus is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Consensus is open about its limits. Its own guide warns that AI can miss nuances, limitations or caveats, that not all studies are equally rigorous, and that you should never copy its summaries into a paper or cite a paper whose abstract you have not read. Oregon State notes it does not search subscription databases such as Web of Science, and SMU says it does not cover scholarly books.","sources":[{"name":"Consensus LibGuide for Academic Research","url":"https://consensus.app/home/resources/consensus-libguide-for-academic-research/"},{"name":"Oregon State University Libraries: Consensus","url":"https://guides.library.oregonstate.edu/consensus"},{"name":"SMU Libraries: Get the most out of Consensus","url":"https://blog.smu.edu/smulibraries/2025/10/03/get-the-most-out-of-consensus-an-ai-academic-search-tool"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"SMU Libraries puts it plainly: use Consensus as a discovery tool, not a decision making tool. You can subscribe to an incident there to get updates by email or text.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Outages do happen, and they tend to hit everything at once. On September 29, 2026, Anthropic's status page reported elevated errors on claude.ai, the desktop and mobile apps, Claude Code, Claude Cowork and the Claude API. The problems started at 14:00 UTC and services were back to normal at 14:59 UTC. During that hour, a second issue also blocked many sign ins, new chats, file uploads and purchases.","sources":[{"name":"Claude Status","url":"https://status.claude.com/incidents/4xvtc2gnq73l"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"During that incident Anthropic asked users who were already signed in not to sign out, and said retrying might work. That is good advice for any outage: logging out and back in can leave you locked out until sign in is fixed.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Earlier in the year, on January 22, 2026, TechRadar tracked another outage in which users saw a message asking them to try again, on both desktop and mobile, while Claude Code had a separate sign in problem. A capacity error: wait a few minutes","text":"If you see \"Due to unexpected capacity constraints, Claude is unable to respond to your message. Please try again soon,\" Claude is busy, not broken. When you get close, Claude shows \"Approaching session limit\" or \"Approaching weekly limit.\" When you hit it, the message tells you when it resets, for example \"5-hour limit reached\" with a time. A length limit: split the work","text":"\"Your message will exceed the length limit for this chat\" means the conversation plus your files is too big. On paid plans with code execution turned on, long chats are summarized automatically.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. A login error: clean up your browser","text":"For errors like \"There was an error logging you in,\" Anthropic lists three steps in order: do not use a VPN, disable browser extensions, and clear your browser cache and cookies. There are also apps for iPhone and Android, and a web app at notes.granola.ai that can view and edit notes but cannot transcribe.","sources":[{"name":"Granola","url":"https://www.granola.ai/"},{"name":"Granola Docs: Transcription","url":"https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/taking-notes/transcription"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to set up Granola","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Install the desktop app","text":"Download Granola from its website. On a Mac, open the downloaded file and drag Granola into your Applications folder. On Windows, run the installer. The Mac app needs macOS 14 or later.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Sign in with Google or Microsoft","text":"Click Sign in and finish in your browser. Granola only supports Google and Microsoft sign-in. Use your work account if you have one, because Granola builds your meeting list from that calendar. When it asks for calendar permissions, choose Select all, then Continue.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Allow audio access","text":"On a Mac, click Allow on the microphone and system audio prompts. Windows grants both automatically. You can review them later in your system's Privacy and Security settings.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Watch the demo meeting","text":"After the first sign-in, Granola opens a short demo meeting that shows the whole flow in about two minutes. After that, your home screen lists upcoming meetings from your calendar.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to take meeting notes with Granola","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Start a note when the call starts","text":"Click the meeting notification, open the meeting from your home screen, or click New Note for a call that is not on your calendar. Granola does not transcribe in the background on its own: a meeting is only transcribed when you have a note open for it.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Type a few cues, not everything","text":"Write down only what matters to you: a decision, a number to check, a name. Granola uses those lines to decide what the summary should focus on. In the transcript, your microphone shows up as Me and the other side as Them, unless speaker names are available.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Stop the transcript yourself","text":"Granola stops when it detects the call has ended, after 15 minutes of silence, or when your computer sleeps. Do not count on that. If you have back-to-back calls, press stop between them, or two meetings can end up in one transcript.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Pick a template","text":"Templates set the structure of the finished notes. During a call, type a forward slash in your notes and choose one. After the notes are generated, click the dropdown arrow on the Enhanced tab and pick another template, and the notes are rewritten in that format. Templates only work in the desktop apps.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Make your own template for each meeting you repeat, such as a weekly team check-in or a sales call. Granola's docs suggest saying what you want from the meeting, how long the notes should be, and which sections to include, such as decisions and action items.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Ask Granola Chat about your meetings","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Granola Chat sits at the bottom of the desktop and iPhone apps. Where you open it decides what it searches: one meeting, a folder, a set of meetings you select, or everything from the home screen. It only knows your meeting notes and files you add, not your email or to-do lists. On the free Basic plan, Chat covers the last 30 days of notes.","sources":[{"name":"Granola Docs: Chatting with your meetings","url":"https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/getting-more-from-your-notes/chatting-with-your-meetings"}]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 1: Before a call","text":"What did we decide in the last meeting with [client name], and what did we promise to send them?","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 2: Right after a call","text":"List every action item from this meeting as a table with the task, the person who owns it and the deadline if one was said. Mark anything that had no owner.","sources":[]},{"kind":"prompt","title":"Prompt 3: Across many meetings","text":"Which topics came up in more than one of these meetings? For each one, give the meetings where it came up and what was said.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If you ask the same thing after every call, save it as a Recipe. Type a forward slash in the chat bar, choose Create a recipe, give it a name and a prompt, and say whether it runs on single meetings or multiple meetings. Recipes run as written and do not support placeholders, so leave the brackets out.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Granola costs","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Granola lists three plans. Basic is free and keeps 30 days of meeting history; it leaves out integrations such as Notion and Zapier, pre-meeting briefs, follow-up emails and API access. Business costs $14 per user per month with unlimited history. Enterprise costs $35 per user per month and adds admin controls such as single sign-on and workspace-wide policies. If you drop from Business to Basic, older notes are hidden, not deleted.","sources":[{"name":"Granola blog: Plans compared","url":"https://granola.ai/blog/granola-pricing-plans-features-roi"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Consent: tell people you are using it","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"No bot in the call also means nobody is told automatically. Granola's own guidance says participants should know when you use an AI notetaker, that recording laws differ by region, and that you should check with your legal or IT team. It also suggests pausing the transcript if a conversation turns sensitive.","sources":[{"name":"Granola Docs: When to use AI notetaking","url":"https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/consent-security-privacy/getting-consent"}]},{"kind":"step","title":"9. Turn on the transparency features","text":"Go to Settings, then Preferences, then Transparency. The automated chat message posts a short notice in the meeting chat when you start transcribing. For Google Meet it needs the Granola browser extension. The Granola Watermark puts a small badge on your camera video while Granola is listening.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What Granola is bad at","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Granola does not save audio or video, so there is nothing to play back when a line in the transcript looks wrong, and it cannot import recordings you already have. On desktop it captures all system audio at once, so music or other sounds on your computer can end up in the transcript. Speakers are often inferred from context, so names can be attributed to the wrong person. The phone apps cannot capture audio from video call apps.","sources":[{"name":"Granola Docs: Transcription","url":"https://docs.granola.ai/help-center/taking-notes/transcription"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Independent reviewers point to the same gaps. A review on the blog of tl;dv, a competitor, called the missing playback a real problem when a transcript in Russian came out poorly. Zack Proser, who uses Granola daily and links to it as an affiliate, recommends checking names, numbers and dates against the transcript for a few minutes after each meeting.","sources":[{"name":"tl;dv: Granola review","url":"https://tldv.io/blog/granola-review/"},{"name":"Zack Proser: Granola AI review","url":"https://zackproser.com/blog/granola-ai-review"}]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"Granola fits people who sit in a lot of video calls, want to stay in the conversation instead of typing, and do not need a recording afterward. It fits less well if you need audio to prove what was said, or if your team has strict rules about where meeting data is processed. Try it on a few ordinary meetings on the free plan, turn on the chat message from day one, and read the first summaries closely before you trust them.","sources":[]}]}

item.title: How to delete all your ChatGPT chats, and what it remembers
item.author: NeuraFeed news desk
item.description: In the sidebar, hover over the chat, click the three dots and choose Delete. Confirm it. Pick Archive instead to hide it without deleting. Open Settings, then Data controls. Next to Delete all chats, click Delete all and confirm. It also clears chats inside your projects. Deleting chats does not erase all memories. Open Personalization to manage them or turn off Enable memory. Sources: OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT, All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account.

item.nf:article: {"kind":"guide","headline":"How to delete all ChatGPT chats, and clear what ChatGPT remembers about you","dek":"Deleting one chat, deleting everything, archiving instead, and the separate memory settings most people forget. Plus what happens to your data after you hit delete.","summary":"To delete all ChatGPT chats, open Settings, go to Data controls and choose Delete all next to Delete all chats, then confirm. Deleting chats does not erase every saved memory, so memories have to be managed separately under Personalization.","seo_title":"How to delete all ChatGPT chats (and your memory)","seo_description":"Steps to delete one ChatGPT chat or all of them, archive instead, clear saved memories, stop training on your chats, and the 30 day deletion rule explained.","answer_summary":"Open ChatGPT Settings, choose Data controls, click Delete all next to Delete all chats and confirm. This removes every conversation, including chats in projects, but not all saved memories, which you manage under Personalization.","tags":["ChatGPT","OpenAI","Privacy","Chat history","Guides"],"paragraphs":[{"kind":"fact","text":"You can delete all ChatGPT chats at once from Settings, under Data controls. One button clears your whole history, including conversations inside projects, according to OpenAI's help center. Deleted chats disappear from your sidebar right away and are permanently removed from OpenAI's systems within 30 days, unless a legal or security exception applies.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/8809935-how-chat-retention-works-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The part most people miss: deleting chats does not wipe what ChatGPT has learned about you. ChatGPT builds memories from your chat history, files and connected apps, and deleting a chat may remove a specific memory but not all of them. Memory has its own settings, covered further down.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Deleted chats cannot be brought back. OpenAI says they cannot be recovered through the app, the API or support. If there is anything you want to keep, export your data first.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Before you delete: export your ChatGPT data","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"1. Request a data export","text":"OpenAI's help center points to Settings, then Data controls, to request a data export. It is also a quick way to see which chats are still stored on your account before you clear them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to delete all ChatGPT chats at once","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"2. Open Settings","text":"On the web, click your profile and choose Settings.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"3. Go to Data controls","text":"Choose Data controls in the left menu of the Settings window.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"4. Click Delete all","text":"Find Delete all chats and click Delete all next to it. Then click Confirm deletion. Every conversation goes, including the ones saved inside projects.","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The same Data controls page has Archive all chats, with an Archive all button and a Confirm archive step. Archiving is not deleting: it moves chats out of the sidebar, and they stay on your account under the normal retention rules.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/8809935-how-chat-retention-works-in-chatgpt"},{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to delete or archive a single chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"5. Hover over the chat in the sidebar","text":"Move your pointer over the conversation in your chat history and click the three dots next to its title.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"6. Choose Delete or Archive","text":"Select Delete and confirm when ChatGPT asks. Select Archive instead if you only want it out of sight. Archiving needs no confirmation.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"7. Find archived chats later","text":"Open Settings, then Data controls, and click Manage next to Archived Chats. From there you can unarchive a chat, which puts it back in your history, or delete it for good.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"If a chat seems to have vanished, check Archived Chats before you assume it was deleted. OpenAI's help center lists that as the first thing to check.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"How to clear ChatGPT memory","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"8. Manage saved memories","text":"Open Personalization from your profile menu. Under Memory summary, select Manage to see what ChatGPT has stored, then update or delete individual memories.","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"9. Turn memory off","text":"In the same Personalization settings, switch off Enable memory. This stops ChatGPT from creating new memories. It does not remove the ones already saved, so delete those first if you want a clean slate.","sources":[]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Images, training and Temporary Chat","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Images can outlive the chat they came from. Deleting a chat generally removes its images, but some may still sit in your Library. To remove them, open Library in the left menu, go to Images, select the pictures with the circle in the bottom right corner of each one, and click Delete.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Clearing your history does not change whether future chats are used to train OpenAI's models. That is a separate switch: in Settings, under Data controls, turn off Improve the model for everyone. It is on by default.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"For conversations you never want saved, use Temporary Chat. These chats do not appear in your history, do not create new memories and are not used to improve OpenAI's models. OpenAI's deletion window of 30 days covers them too.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"What happens after you delete","sources":[]},{"kind":"fact","text":"Chats are removed from view immediately and permanently deleted from OpenAI's systems within 30 days. OpenAI names two exceptions: a chat that was already de-identified and disconnected from your account, and a chat OpenAI must keep for security or legal reasons. Deleting a conversation also removes synced data from connected apps that was kept in it, while disconnecting an app only stops future access.","sources":[{"name":"OpenAI Help Center: How to Delete and Archive Chats in ChatGPT","url":"https://help-lb.openai.com/en/articles/8809935-how-chat-retention-works-in-chatgpt"}]},{"kind":"fact","text":"The legal exception is not theoretical. All About Cookies notes that a federal court order in a copyright lawsuit brought by publishers including The New York Times required OpenAI to produce about 20 million conversations, with personal details removed or masked.","sources":[{"name":"All About Cookies: How to delete your ChatGPT history and account","url":"https://allaboutcookies.org/delete-chatgpt-history"}]},{"kind":"heading","text":"Deleting your whole ChatGPT account","sources":[]},{"kind":"step","title":"10. Delete the account (optional)","text":"Open Settings, choose Account, and click Delete under Delete account. Enter your account email, type DELETE and click Permanently delete my account. You cannot sign up again with the same email or phone number for 30 days.","sources":[]},{"kind":"tip","text":"Deleting your account does not cancel a subscription you bought through the App Store or Google Play. Cancel it there first. All About Cookies also suggests deleting chats and images before deleting the account, since OpenAI does not spell out that account deletion removes them.","sources":[]},{"kind":"analysis","text":"The honest summary: Delete all chats is fast and thorough for your history, but it is only one of three switches. If you want ChatGPT to forget you, clear your memories under Personalization, and if you want future chats kept out of training, turn off Improve the model for everyone. These steps are written for the web version; menu names may look slightly different in the apps.","sources":[]}]}
